======================================================================

SOFTWARE SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Software Services Agreement (this "Agreement") is entered into as of March 3, 2025 (the "Effective Date") by and between Granite Peak Foods Inc., a Texas corporation ("Vendor"), and Wrenfield Outdoor Co., a Delaware corporation ("Client").

RECITALS. Client wishes to obtain, and Vendor wishes to provide, the services described in this Agreement on the terms set out below.

SECTION 1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Documentation" means the user guides, specifications and operating manuals that Vendor makes generally available for the Services, as updated from time to time.
1.2 "Affiliate" means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a party, where "control" means ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting interests of the entity.
1.3 "Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or a day on which national banks in Atlanta are authorized to close.
1.4 "Personnel" means the employees, agents and permitted subcontractors of a party who perform obligations under this Agreement.

SECTION 2. COUNTERPARTS
2.1 This Agreement may be signed in counterparts, including by electronic signature, each of which is an original and all of which together are one instrument.

SECTION 3. ENTIRE AGREEMENT AND AMENDMENT
3.1 This Agreement, including its Schedules and each SOW, is the entire agreement of the parties on its subject and supersedes all prior proposals and understandings.
3.2 This Agreement may be amended only by a written instrument signed by authorized representatives of both parties.

SECTION 4. TERMINATION
4.1 Either party may terminate this Agreement or any SOW on written notice if the other party materially breaches it and fails to cure the breach within 45 days after receiving written notice describing it.
4.2 Either party may terminate this Agreement immediately on written notice if the other party becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, or has a receiver appointed for its business.
4.3 Client may terminate any SOW for convenience on 180 days' written notice, paying for Services performed up to the effective date of termination.

SECTION 5. SEVERABILITY AND WAIVER
5.1 If any provision of this Agreement is held invalid, the remaining provisions remain in effect. A failure to enforce a provision is not a waiver of it.

SECTION 6. TAXES
6.1 Fees exclude sales, use, value added and similar taxes. Client shall pay any such taxes that Vendor is required to collect, other than taxes on Vendor's net income, property or employees.
6.2 If Client is required by law to withhold tax from a payment, it shall pay the amount withheld to the relevant authority and provide Vendor with evidence of payment within 20 days.

SECTION 7. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY
7.1 Upon payment in full of the applicable fees, Client shall own all deliverables created specifically for Client under an SOW, and Vendor hereby assigns to Client all rights in them.
7.2 Vendor retains all rights in its pre-existing materials, tools and know-how, and in any general improvements to them. To the extent any of them is incorporated in a deliverable, Vendor grants Client a perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use it as part of that deliverable.

SECTION 8. NOTICES
8.1 Notices under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered by hand, by nationally recognized overnight courier, or by email with confirmation of receipt, to the addresses set out on the signature page or as later updated by notice.
8.2 A notice is effective on receipt, or if delivered by courier, 2 Business Day(s) after dispatch.

SECTION 9. EFFECT OF TERMINATION
9.1 On termination, Client shall pay all fees for Services performed through the effective date of termination, and each party shall return the other's Confidential Information as provided in this Agreement.
9.2 At Client's request, Vendor shall provide reasonable transition assistance for up to 20 days after termination, at the rates then in effect.

SECTION 10. VENUE
10.1 Each party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in Fairfax County, Virginia, for any action arising out of or relating to this Agreement, and waives any objection to venue in those courts.

SECTION 11. CONFIDENTIALITY
11.1 Each party (the "Recipient") shall keep confidential all non-public information disclosed by the other party (the "Discloser") that is marked confidential or would reasonably be understood to be confidential ("Confidential Information"), and shall use it only to perform or receive the benefit of this Agreement.
11.2 The Recipient may disclose Confidential Information to its Personnel and professional advisers who need to know it and are bound by obligations of confidentiality no less protective than this Section.
11.3 These obligations continue for two (2) years after the expiration or termination of this Agreement, and for trade secrets for as long as they remain trade secrets under applicable law.
11.4 Within 20 days after a written request, the Recipient shall return or destroy the Discloser's Confidential Information, except for copies retained in routine backups or as required by law.

SECTION 12. COMPLIANCE WITH LAWS
12.1 Each party shall comply with all laws applicable to its performance of this Agreement, including anti-bribery laws and the export control and economic sanctions laws of the United States.
12.2 Neither party shall export, re-export or transfer any deliverable in violation of the export control laws of the United States or of any other applicable jurisdiction.

SECTION 13. DATA PROTECTION
13.1 To the extent Vendor processes personal data on behalf of Client, it shall do so only on Client's documented instructions and in accordance with the data processing terms in Schedule D.
13.2 Vendor shall notify Client without undue delay, and in any event within 24 hours, after becoming aware of a security incident affecting Client's personal data.
13.3 Vendor shall retain Client's data for no longer than 60 days after the end of the applicable SOW, after which it shall securely delete that data unless retention is required by law.

SECTION 14. INDEPENDENT CONTRACTORS
14.1 The parties are independent contractors. Nothing in this Agreement creates a partnership, joint venture, agency or employment relationship between them.

SECTION 15. INFORMATION SECURITY
15.1 Vendor shall maintain administrative, physical and technical safeguards designed to protect Client's data, consistent with a recognized industry framework such as ISO/IEC 27001 or the NIST Cybersecurity Framework.
15.2 Vendor shall perform vulnerability scans of systems that process Client's data at least every 60 days and remediate critical findings within 120 days.

SECTION 16. INSURANCE
16.1 Vendor shall maintain, with insurers rated A- or better, commercial general liability insurance of at least five million dollars ($5,000,000) per occurrence, professional liability insurance of at least five million dollars ($5,000,000) per claim, and workers' compensation insurance as required by law.
16.2 Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request and give Client at least 60 days' notice before any required policy is cancelled or materially reduced.

SECTION 17. STATEMENTS OF WORK
17.1 The specific services, deliverables, milestones and fees for each engagement will be set out in a statement of work signed by authorized representatives of both parties (each, an "SOW"). Each SOW incorporates the terms of this Agreement.
17.2 Vendor shall not begin work under an SOW until it has been signed by both parties. Work performed before signature is at Vendor's own risk and expense.
17.3 Each SOW will identify a project manager for each party. The project managers will meet at least every 30 days to review progress, risks and open decisions.
17.4 If an SOW conflicts with this Agreement, this Agreement controls, unless the SOW expressly identifies by section number the provision of this Agreement that it overrides.

SECTION 18. ACCEPTANCE
18.1 Client shall test each deliverable against the acceptance criteria in the applicable SOW within 15 Business Days of delivery and notify Vendor in writing of acceptance or of any non-conformity.
18.2 If Client reports a non-conformity, Vendor shall correct it and redeliver within 120 days, and the acceptance procedure shall be repeated. If a deliverable fails acceptance three (3) times, Client may terminate the applicable SOW and recover the fees paid for that deliverable.

SECTION 19. TERM AND RENEWAL
19.1 The initial term of this Agreement is eighteen (18) months from the Effective Date (the "Initial Term").
19.2 After the Initial Term, this Agreement renews automatically for successive periods of twelve (12) months each unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal at least one hundred eighty (180) days before the end of the then-current term.

SECTION 20. ASSIGNMENT
20.1 Neither party may assign this Agreement without the other party's prior written consent, except to an Affiliate or to a successor to all or substantially all of its business to which this Agreement relates, on written notice to the other party.

SECTION 21. DISPUTE ESCALATION
21.1 The parties shall first attempt to resolve any dispute through their project managers. If unresolved within 120 days, either party may escalate it to an executive of each party, who shall meet within a further 120 days.
21.2 Nothing in this Section prevents a party from seeking urgent injunctive relief.

SECTION 22. INDEMNIFICATION
22.1 Vendor shall defend Client against any third-party claim alleging that a deliverable infringes a patent, copyright or trademark, and pay any damages finally awarded or agreed in settlement.
22.2 The indemnified party shall give prompt notice of the claim, allow the indemnifying party to control its defense, and provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense.

SECTION 23. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY
23.1 Neither party is liable for any indirect, incidental, special or consequential damages, or for lost profits, even if advised of their possibility.
23.2 Except for the excluded claims below, each party's aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed two million dollars ($2,000,000).
23.3 The limitation above does not apply to a party's indemnification obligations or to its breach of the confidentiality obligations in this Agreement, for which that party's aggregate liability shall not exceed seven million five hundred thousand dollars ($7,500,000).

SECTION 24. PUBLICITY
24.1 Neither party shall use the other's name or logo in any publicity, customer list or marketing material without the other's prior written consent.

SECTION 25. CHANGE CONTROL
25.1 Either party may request a change to the scope, schedule or fees of an SOW by written change request. Vendor shall respond within 5 Business Days with an estimate of the impact on schedule and fees.
25.2 No change is binding until a change order describing it is signed by both parties. Vendor is not obliged to perform any change until that change order is signed.

SECTION 26. GOVERNING LAW
26.1 This Agreement and any dispute arising out of it are governed by the laws of the State of Oregon, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules.

SECTION 27. EXPENSES
27.1 Client shall reimburse Vendor for reasonable travel and out-of-pocket expenses that Client has approved in writing in advance, at cost and without mark-up, provided they comply with Client's travel policy as provided to Vendor.
27.2 Expense claims must be submitted within 30 days after the expense is incurred, with receipts for any single item above two hundred fifty dollars ($250).

SECTION 28. FORCE MAJEURE
28.1 Neither party is liable for any delay or failure to perform caused by events beyond its reasonable control, including fire, flood, war, epidemic, governmental action or failure of public utilities, provided it gives prompt notice and uses reasonable efforts to resume performance.
28.2 If a force majeure event prevents performance for more than 15 consecutive days, either party may terminate the affected SOW on written notice.

SECTION 29. FEES AND INVOICING
29.1 Client shall pay all undisputed amounts within 120 days after the date of Vendor's invoice. Invoices shall be issued monthly in arrears unless an SOW states otherwise.
29.2 Amounts not paid when due bear interest at the lesser of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month and the highest rate permitted by law, from the due date until paid.
29.3 Client may withhold any amount it disputes in good faith by notifying Vendor of the dispute within 60 days of the invoice date, with reasonable detail of the reasons. The parties shall work together to resolve any dispute promptly.

SECTION 30. NON-SOLICITATION
30.1 During the term of this Agreement and for twelve (12) months after it ends, neither party shall solicit for employment any employee of the other party who was directly involved in performing this Agreement, except through general advertisements not targeted at such employees.

SECTION 31. PERSONNEL AND SUBCONTRACTING
31.1 Vendor shall assign Personnel with the skills and experience reasonably required to perform the Services. Vendor may replace key Personnel named in an SOW only with Client's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
31.2 Vendor may use subcontractors only with Client's prior written consent. Vendor remains responsible for the acts and omissions of its subcontractors as if they were its own.
31.3 Vendor shall ensure that its Personnel comply with Client's reasonable site, security and safety rules when on Client's premises.

SECTION 32. AUDIT
32.1 Client may, on 10 days' written notice and no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, audit Vendor's records relating to fees charged under this Agreement.
32.2 Vendor shall keep those records for at least seven (7) years after the fees are invoiced. If an audit shows an overcharge of more than five percent (5%), Vendor shall bear the reasonable cost of the audit.

SECTION 33. WARRANTIES
33.1 Vendor warrants that the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with generally accepted industry standards, and that each deliverable will conform in all material respects to its specifications for 90 days after acceptance.
33.2 Client's exclusive remedy for breach of the warranty in this Section is for Vendor to re-perform the non-conforming Services or, if Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable time, a refund of the fees paid for them.
33.3 EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY STATED IN THIS AGREEMENT, NEITHER PARTY MAKES ANY OTHER WARRANTY, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING ANY IMPLIED WARRANTY OF MERCHANTABILITY OR FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.

Effective Date by and between Corvane Security Group Holdings, Inc., a Ohio
corporation ("Contractor"), and Ironleaf Media LLP, a Minnesota limited
liability partnership ("Company").

RECITALS. Company wishes to obtain, and Contractor wishes to provide, the ser-
vices described in this Agreement on the terms set out below.

SECTION 1. DEFINITIONS

which national banks in Atlanta are authorized to close.
1.2 "Effective Date" means March 14, 2022.
1.3 "Renewal Term" means a period of twelve (12) months.
1.4 "Documentation" means the user guides, specifications and operating
manuals that Contractor makes generally available for the Services, as updated
from time to time.
1.5 "Non-Renewal Notice Period" means ninety (90) days.
1.6 "Personnel" means the employees, agents and permitted subcontractors of a
party who perform obligations under this Agreement.
1.7 "Affiliate" means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is
controlled by, or is under common control with a party, where "control" means
ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting interests of the
entity.

SECTION 2. STATEMENTS OF WORK

ent will be set out in a statement of work signed by authorized
representatives of both parties (each, an "SOW"). Each SOW incorporates the
terms of this Agreement.

both parties. Work performed before signature is at Contractor's own risk and
expense.
2.3 Each SOW will identify a project manager for each party. The project
managers will meet at least every 30 days to review progress, risks and open
decisions.

the SOW expressly identifies by section number the provision of this Agreement
that it overrides.

signature, each of which ls an original and all of which together are one ins-
trument.

TECHNOLOGY SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Technology Services Agreement (this "Agreement") is entered into as of May 11, 2025 (the "Effective Date") by and between Kitebridge Supply Inc., a Illinois corporation ("Vendor"), and Pellucid Logistics LLC, a Delaware limited liability company ("Client").

RECITALS. Client wishes to obtain, and Vendor wishes to provide, the services described in this Agreement on the terms set out below.

SECTION 1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Documentation" means the user guides, specifications and operating manuals that Vendor makes generally available for the Services, as updated from time to time.
1.2 "Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or a day on which national banks in New York are authorized to close.
1.3 "Affiliate" means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a party, where "control" means ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting interests of the entity.
1.4 "Personnel" means the employees, agents and permitted subcontractors of a party who perform obligations under this Agreement.

SECTION 2. ENTIRE AGREEMENT AND AMENDMENT
2.1 This Agreement, including its Schedules and each SOW, is the entire agreement of the parties on its subject and supersedes all prior proposals and understandings.
2.2 This Agreement may be amended only by a written instrument signed by authorized representatives of both parties.

SECTION 3. TERMINATION
3.1 Either party may terminate this Agreement or any SOW on written notice if the other party materially breaches it and fails to cure the breach within 20 days after receiving written notice describing it.
3.2 Either party may terminate this Agreement immediately on written notice if the other party becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, or has a receiver appointed for its business.
3.3 Client may terminate any SOW for convenience on 30 days' written notice, paying for Services performed up to the effective date of termination.

SECTION 4. FORCE MAJEURE
4.1 Neither party is liable for any delay or failure to perform caused by events beyond its reasonable control, including fire, flood, war, epidemic, governmental action or failure of public utilities, provided it gives prompt notice and uses reasonable efforts to resume performance.
4.2 If a force majeure event prevents performance for more than 15 consecutive days, either party may terminate the affected SOW on written notice.

SECTION 5. NOTICES
5.1 Notices under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered by hand, by nationally recognized overnight courier, or by email with confirmation of receipt, to the addresses set out on the signature page or as later updated by notice.
5.2 A notice is effective on receipt, or if delivered by courier, 1 Business Day(s) after dispatch.

SECTION 6. PUBLICITY
6.1 Neither party shall use the other's name or logo in any publicity, customer list or marketing material without the other's prior written consent.

SECTION 7. NON-SOLICITATION
7.1 During the term of this Agreement and for twelve (12) months after it ends, neither party shall solicit for employment any employee of the other party who was directly involved in performing this Agreement, except through general advertisements not targeted at such employees.

SECTION 8. COMPLIANCE WITH LAWS
8.1 Each party shall comply with all laws applicable to its performance of this Agreement, including anti-bribery laws and the export control and economic sanctions laws of the United States.
8.2 Neither party shall export, re-export or transfer any deliverable in violation of the export control laws of the United States or of any other applicable jurisdiction.

SECTION 9. ACCEPTANCE
9.1 Client shall test each deliverable against the acceptance criteria in the applicable SOW within 10 Business Days of delivery and notify Vendor in writing of acceptance or of any non-conformity.
9.2 If Client reports a non-conformity, Vendor shall correct it and redeliver within 20 days, and the acceptance procedure shall be repeated. If a deliverable fails acceptance three (3) times, Client may terminate the applicable SOW and recover the fees paid for that deliverable.

SECTION 10. INDEPENDENT CONTRACTORS
10.1 The parties are independent contractors. Nothing in this Agreement creates a partnership, joint venture, agency or employment relationship between them.

SECTION 11. EFFECT OF TERMINATION
11.1 On termination, Client shall pay all fees for Services performed through the effective date of termination, and each party shall return the other's Confidential Information as provided in this Agreement.
11.2 At Client's request, Vendor shall provide reasonable transition assistance for up to 120 days after termination, at the rates then in effect.

SECTION 12. AUDIT
12.1 Client may, on 20 days' written notice and no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, audit Vendor's records relating to fees charged under this Agreement.
12.2 Vendor shall keep those records for at least seven (7) years after the fees are invoiced. If an audit shows an overcharge of more than five percent (5%), Vendor shall bear the reasonable cost of the audit.

SECTION 13. INFORMATION SECURITY
13.1 Vendor shall maintain administrative, physical and technical safeguards designed to protect Client's data, consistent with a recognized industry framework such as ISO/IEC 27001 or the NIST Cybersecurity Framework.
13.2 Vendor shall perform vulnerability scans of systems that process Client's data at least every 10 days and remediate critical findings within 10 days.

SECTION 14. STATEMENTS OF WORK
14.1 The specific services, deliverables, milestones and fees for each engagement will be set out in a statement of work signed by authorized representatives of both parties (each, an "SOW"). Each SOW incorporates the terms of this Agreement.
14.2 Vendor shall not begin work under an SOW until it has been signed by both parties. Work performed before signature is at Vendor's own risk and expense.
14.3 Each SOW will identify a project manager for each party. The project managers will meet at least every 7 days to review progress, risks and open decisions.
14.4 If an SOW conflicts with this Agreement, this Agreement controls, unless the SOW expressly identifies by section number the provision of this Agreement that it overrides.

SECTION 15. COUNTERPARTS
15.1 This Agreement may be signed in counterparts, including by electronic signature, each of which is an original and all of which together are one instrument.

SECTION 16. SEVERABILITY AND WAIVER
16.1 If any provision of this Agreement is held invalid, the remaining provisions remain in effect. A failure to enforce a provision is not a waiver of it.

SECTION 17. ASSIGNMENT
17.1 Neither party may assign this Agreement without the other party's prior written consent, except to an Affiliate or to a successor to all or substantially all of its business to which this Agreement relates, on written notice to the other party.

SECTION 18. INDEMNIFICATION
18.1 Vendor shall defend Client against any third-party claim alleging that a deliverable infringes a patent, copyright or trademark, and pay any damages finally awarded or agreed in settlement.
18.2 The indemnified party shall give prompt notice of the claim, allow the indemnifying party to control its defense, and provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense.

SECTION 19. TERM AND RENEWAL
19.1 The initial term of this Agreement is eighteen (18) months from the Effective Date (the "Initial Term").
19.2 After the Initial Term, this Agreement renews automatically for successive periods of twelve (12) months each unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal at least thirty (30) days before the end of the then-current term.

SECTION 20. TAXES
20.1 Fees exclude sales, use, value added and similar taxes. Client shall pay any such taxes that Vendor is required to collect, other than taxes on Vendor's net income, property or employees.
20.2 If Client is required by law to withhold tax from a payment, it shall pay the amount withheld to the relevant authority and provide Vendor with evidence of payment within 90 days.

SECTION 21. WARRANTIES
21.1 Vendor warrants that the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with generally accepted industry standards, and that each deliverable will conform in all material respects to its specifications for 120 days after acceptance.
21.2 Client's exclusive remedy for breach of the warranty in this Section is for Vendor to re-perform the non-conforming Services or, if Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable time, a refund of the fees paid for them.
21.3 EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY STATED IN THIS AGREEMENT, NEITHER PARTY MAKES ANY OTHER WARRANTY, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING ANY IMPLIED WARRANTY OF MERCHANTABILITY OR FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.

SECTION 22. DISPUTE ESCALATION
22.1 The parties shall first attempt to resolve any dispute through their project managers. If unresolved within 30 days, either party may escalate it to an executive of each party, who shall meet within a further 120 days.
22.2 Nothing in this Section prevents a party from seeking urgent injunctive relief.

SECTION 23. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY
23.1 Neither party is liable for any indirect, incidental, special or consequential damages, or for lost profits, even if advised of their possibility.
23.2 Except for the excluded claims below, each party's aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the fees paid or payable by Client under this Agreement in the eighteen (18) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim; provided, however, that in no event shall such aggregate liability exceed one million five hundred thousand dollars ($1,500,000).
23.3 The limitation above does not apply to a party's indemnification obligations or to its breach of the confidentiality obligations in this Agreement, for which that party's aggregate liability shall not exceed seven million five hundred thousand dollars ($7,500,000).

SECTION 24. CONFIDENTIALITY
24.1 Each party (the "Recipient") shall keep confidential all non-public information disclosed by the other party (the "Discloser") that is marked confidential or would reasonably be understood to be confidential ("Confidential Information"), and shall use it only to perform or receive the benefit of this Agreement.
24.2 The Recipient may disclose Confidential Information to its Personnel and professional advisers who need to know it and are bound by obligations of confidentiality no less protective than this Section.
24.3 These obligations continue for three (3) years after the expiration or termination of this Agreement, and for trade secrets for as long as they remain trade secrets under applicable law.
24.4 Within 15 days after a written request, the Recipient shall return or destroy the Discloser's Confidential Information, except for copies retained in routine backups or as required by law.

SECTION 25. FEES AND INVOICING
25.1 Client shall pay all undisputed amounts within 45 days after the date of Vendor's invoice. Invoices shall be issued monthly in arrears unless an SOW states otherwise.
25.2 Amounts not paid when due bear interest at the lesser of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month and the highest rate permitted by law, from the due date until paid.
25.3 Client may withhold any amount it disputes in good faith by notifying Vendor of the dispute within 120 days of the invoice date, with reasonable detail of the reasons. The parties shall work together to resolve any dispute promptly.

SECTION 26. GOVERNING LAW
26.1 This Agreement and any dispute arising out of it are governed by the laws of the State of California, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules.

SECTION 27. INSURANCE
27.1 Vendor shall maintain, with insurers rated A- or better, commercial general liability insurance of at least three million dollars ($3,000,000) per occurrence, professional liability insurance of at least three million dollars ($3,000,000) per claim, and workers' compensation insurance as required by law.
27.2 Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request and give Client at least 15 days' notice before any required policy is cancelled or materially reduced.

SECTION 28. VENUE
28.1 Each party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in San Francisco County, California, for any action arising out of or relating to this Agreement, and waives any objection to venue in those courts.

SECTION 29. DATA PROTECTION
29.1 To the extent Vendor processes personal data on behalf of Client, it shall do so only on Client's documented instructions and in accordance with the data processing terms in Schedule D.
29.2 Vendor shall notify Client without undue delay, and in any event within 48 hours, after becoming aware of a security incident affecting Client's personal data.
29.3 Vendor shall retain Client's data for no longer than 60 days after the end of the applicable SOW, after which it shall securely delete that data unless retention is required by law.

SECTION 30. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY
30.1 Upon payment in full of the applicable fees, Client shall own all deliverables created specifically for Client under an SOW, and Vendor hereby assigns to Client all rights in them.
30.2 Vendor retains all rights in its pre-existing materials, tools and know-how, and in any general improvements to them. To the extent any of them is incorporated in a deliverable, Vendor grants Client a perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use it as part of that deliverable.

SECTION 31. CHANGE CONTROL
31.1 Either party may request a change to the scope, schedule or fees of an SOW by written change request. Vendor shall respond within 5 Business Days with an estimate of the impact on schedule and fees.
31.2 No change is binding until a change order describing it is signed by both parties. Vendor is not obliged to perform any change until that change order is signed.

SECTION 32. EXPENSES
32.1 Client shall reimburse Vendor for reasonable travel and out-of-pocket expenses that Client has approved in writing in advance, at cost and without mark-up, provided they comply with Client's travel policy as provided to Vendor.
32.2 Expense claims must be submitted within 20 days after the expense is incurred, with receipts for any single item above two hundred fifty dollars ($250).

SECTION 33. PERSONNEL AND SUBCONTRACTING
33.1 Vendor shall assign Personnel with the skills and experience reasonably required to perform the Services. Vendor may replace key Personnel named in an SOW only with Client's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
33.2 Vendor may use subcontractors only with Client's prior written consent. Vendor remains responsible for the acts and omissions of its subcontractors as if they were its own.
33.3 Vendor shall ensure that its Personnel comply with Client's reasonable site, security and safety rules when on Client's premises.

This Professional Services Agreement (this "Agreement") is entered into as of
November 12, 2025 (the "Effective Date") by and between Delmont Digital LLP, a
Massachusetts limited liability partnership ("Supplier"), and Granite Peak
Logistics LLP, a Virginia limited liability partnership ("Buyer").

RECITALS. Buyer wishes to obtain, and Supplier wishes to provide, the services
described in this Agreement on the terms set out below.

SECTION 1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Affiliate" means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is
controlled by, or is under common control with a party, where "control" means
ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting interests of the
entity.
1.2 "Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or a day on
which national banks in Chicago are authorized to close.
1.3 "Documentation" means the user guides, specifications and operating
manuals that Supplier makes generally available for the Services, as updated
from time to time.
1.4 "Personnel" means the employees, agents and permitted subcontractors of a
party who perform obligations under this Agreement.

SECTION 2. PERSONNEL AND SUBCONTRACTING
2.1 Supplier shall assign Personnel with the skills and experience reasonably
required to perform the Services. Supplier may replace key Personnel named in
an SOW only with Buyer's prior written consent, which shall not be
unreasonably withheld.
2.2 Supplier may use subcontractors only with Buyer's prior written consent.
Supplier remains responsible for the acts and omissions of its subcontractors
as if they were its own.
2.3 Supplier shall ensure that its Personnel comply with Buyer's reasonable
site, security and safety rules when on Buyer's premises.

SECTION 3. FEES AND INVOICING
3.1 Buyer shall pay all undisputed amounts within 15 days after the date of
Supplier's invoice. Invoices shall be issued monthly in arrears unless an SOW
states otherwise.
3.2 Amounts not paid when due bear interest at the lesser of one and one-half
percent (1.5%) per month and the highest rate permitted by law, from the due
date until paid.
3.3 Buyer may withhold any amount it disputes in good faith by notifying
Supplier of the dispute within 120 days of the invoice date, with reasonable
detail of the reasons. The parties shall work together to resolve any dispute
promptly.

SECTION 4. STATEMENTS OF WORK
4.1 The specific services, deliverables, milestones and fces for each
engagement will be set out in a statement of work signed by authorized repres-

entatives of both parties (each, an "SOW"). Each SOW incorporates the terms of

expense.
4.3 Each SOW will identify a project manager for each party. The project
managers will meet at least every 14 days to review progress, risks and open
decisions.
4.4 If an SOW conflicts with this Agreement, this Agreement controls, unless
the SOW expressly identifies by section number the provision of this Agreement
that it overrides.

SECTION 5. AUDIT
5.1 Buyer may, on 45 days' written notice and no more than once in any twelve
(12) month period, audit Supplier's records relating to fees charged under
this Agreement.
5.2 Supplier shall keep those records for at least seven (7) years after the
fees are invoiced. If an audit shows an overcharge of more than five percent
(5%), Supplier shall bear the reasonable cost of the audit.

SECTION 6. TERMINATION
6.1 Either party may terminate this Agreement or any SOW on written notice if
the other party materially breaches it and fails to cure the breach within 20
days after receiving written notice describing it.
6.2 Either party may terminate this Agreement immediately on written notice if
the other party becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for the benefit
of creditors, or has a receiver appointed for its business.
6.3 Buyer may terminate any SOW for convenience on 90 days' written notice,
paying for Services performed up to the effective date of termination.

eral liability insurance of at least two rnillion dollars ($2,000,000) per

($5,000,000) per claim, and workers' compensation insurance as required by

TECHNOLOGY SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Technology Services Agreement (this "Agreement") is entered into as of August 31, 2023 (the "Effective Date") by and between Marlow Supply Inc., a Massachusetts corporation ("Supplier"), and Tidewater Security Group LLP, a Georgia limited liability partnership ("Buyer").

RECITALS. Buyer wishes to obtain, and Supplier wishes to provide, the services described in this Agreement on the terms set out below.

SECTION 1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Affiliate" means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a party, where "control" means ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting interests of the entity.
1.2 "Non-Renewal Notice Period" means thirty (30) days.
1.3 "Renewal Term" means a period of twelve (12) months.
1.4 "Personnel" means the employees, agents and permitted subcontractors of a party who perform obligations under this Agreement.
1.5 "Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or a day on which national banks in Dallas are authorized to close.
1.6 "Documentation" means the user guides, specifications and operating manuals that Supplier makes generally available for the Services, as updated from time to time.

SECTION 2. NON-SOLICITATION
2.1 During the term of this Agreement and for six (6) months after it ends, neither party shall solicit for employment any employee of the other party who was directly involved in performing this Agreement, except through general advertisements not targeted at such employees.

SECTION 3. SEVERABILITY AND WAIVER
3.1 If any provision of this Agreement is held invalid, the remaining provisions remain in effect. A failure to enforce a provision is not a waiver of it.

SECTION 4. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY
4.1 Upon payment in full of the applicable fees, Buyer shall own all deliverables created specifically for Buyer under an SOW, and Supplier hereby assigns to Buyer all rights in them.
4.2 Supplier retains all rights in its pre-existing materials, tools and know-how, and in any general improvements to them. To the extent any of them is incorporated in a deliverable, Supplier grants Buyer a perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use it as part of that deliverable.

SECTION 5. CONFIDENTIALITY
5.1 Each party (the "Recipient") shall keep confidential all non-public information disclosed by the other party (the "Discloser") that is marked confidential or would reasonably be understood to be confidential ("Confidential Information"), and shall use it only to perform or receive the benefit of this Agreement.
5.2 The Recipient may disclose Confidential Information to its Personnel and professional advisers who need to know it and are bound by obligations of confidentiality no less protective than this Section.
5.3 These obligations continue for five (5) years after the expiration or termination of this Agreement, and for trade secrets for as long as they remain trade secrets under applicable law.
5.4 Within 90 days after a written request, the Recipient shall return or destroy the Discloser's Confidential Information, except for copies retained in routine backups or as required by law.

SECTION 6. WARRANTIES
6.1 Supplier warrants that the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with generally accepted industry standards, and that each deliverable will conform in all material respects to its specifications for 90 days after acceptance.
6.2 Buyer's exclusive remedy for breach of the warranty in this Section is for Supplier to re-perform the non-conforming Services or, if Supplier cannot do so within a reasonable time, a refund of the fees paid for them.
6.3 EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY STATED IN THIS AGREEMENT, NEITHER PARTY MAKES ANY OTHER WARRANTY, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING ANY IMPLIED WARRANTY OF MERCHANTABILITY OR FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.

SECTION 7. TERMINATION
7.1 Either party may terminate this Agreement or any SOW on written notice if the other party materially breaches it and fails to cure the breach within 15 days after receiving written notice describing it.
7.2 Either party may terminate this Agreement immediately on written notice if the other party becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, or has a receiver appointed for its business.
7.3 Buyer may terminate any SOW for convenience on 45 days' written notice, paying for Services performed up to the effective date of termination.

SECTION 8. FEES AND INVOICING
8.1 Buyer shall pay all undisputed amounts within 15 days after the date of Supplier's invoice. Invoices shall be issued monthly in arrears unless an SOW states otherwise.
8.2 Amounts not paid when due bear interest at the lesser of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month and the highest rate permitted by law, from the due date until paid.
8.3 Buyer may withhold any amount it disputes in good faith by notifying Supplier of the dispute within 10 days of the invoice date, with reasonable detail of the reasons. The parties shall work together to resolve any dispute promptly.

SECTION 9. DISPUTE ESCALATION
9.1 The parties shall first attempt to resolve any dispute through their project managers. If unresolved within 60 days, either party may escalate it to an executive of each party, who shall meet within a further 120 days.
9.2 Nothing in this Section prevents a party from seeking urgent injunctive relief.

SECTION 10. INSURANCE
10.1 Supplier shall maintain, with insurers rated A- or better, commercial general liability insurance of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000) per occurrence, professional liability insurance of at least five million dollars ($5,000,000) per claim, and workers' compensation insurance as required by law.
10.2 Supplier shall provide certificates of insurance on request and give Buyer at least 90 days' notice before any required policy is cancelled or materially reduced.

SECTION 11. EFFECT OF TERMINATION
11.1 On termination, Buyer shall pay all fees for Services performed through the effective date of termination, and each party shall return the other's Confidential Information as provided in this Agreement.
11.2 At Buyer's request, Supplier shall provide reasonable transition assistance for up to 10 days after termination, at the rates then in effect.

SECTION 12. INFORMATION SECURITY
12.1 Supplier shall maintain administrative, physical and technical safeguards designed to protect Buyer's data, consistent with a recognized industry framework such as ISO/IEC 27001 or the NIST Cybersecurity Framework.
12.2 Supplier shall perform vulnerability scans of systems that process Buyer's data at least every 20 days and remediate critical findings within 30 days.

SECTION 13. TAXES
13.1 Fees exclude sales, use, value added and similar taxes. Buyer shall pay any such taxes that Supplier is required to collect, other than taxes on Supplier's net income, property or employees.
13.2 If Buyer is required by law to withhold tax from a payment, it shall pay the amount withheld to the relevant authority and provide Supplier with evidence of payment within 180 days.

SECTION 14. COUNTERPARTS
14.1 This Agreement may be signed in counterparts, including by electronic signature, each of which is an original and all of which together are one instrument.

SECTION 15. ASSIGNMENT
15.1 Neither party may assign this Agreement without the other party's prior written consent, except to an Affiliate or to a successor to all or substantially all of its business to which this Agreement relates, on written notice to the other party.

SECTION 16. CHANGE CONTROL
16.1 Either party may request a change to the scope, schedule or fees of an SOW by written change request. Supplier shall respond within 10 Business Days with an estimate of the impact on schedule and fees.
16.2 No change is binding until a change order describing it is signed by both parties. Supplier is not obliged to perform any change until that change order is signed.

SECTION 17. ACCEPTANCE
17.1 Buyer shall test each deliverable against the acceptance criteria in the applicable SOW within 15 Business Days of delivery and notify Supplier in writing of acceptance or of any non-conformity.
17.2 If Buyer reports a non-conformity, Supplier shall correct it and redeliver within 45 days, and the acceptance procedure shall be repeated. If a deliverable fails acceptance three (3) times, Buyer may terminate the applicable SOW and recover the fees paid for that deliverable.

SECTION 18. VENUE
18.1 Each party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in Denver County, Colorado, for any action arising out of or relating to this Agreement, and waives any objection to venue in those courts.

SECTION 19. TERM AND RENEWAL
19.1 The initial term of this Agreement is thirty-six (36) months from the Effective Date (the "Initial Term").
19.2 After the Initial Term, this Agreement renews automatically for successive Renewal Terms unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal no later than the Non-Renewal Notice Period before the end of the then-current term.

SECTION 20. INDEPENDENT CONTRACTORS
20.1 The parties are independent contractors. Nothing in this Agreement creates a partnership, joint venture, agency or employment relationship between them.

SECTION 21. INDEMNIFICATION
21.1 Supplier shall defend Buyer against any third-party claim alleging that a deliverable infringes a patent, copyright or trademark, and pay any damages finally awarded or agreed in settlement.
21.2 The indemnified party shall give prompt notice of the claim, allow the indemnifying party to control its defense, and provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense.

SECTION 22. COMPLIANCE WITH LAWS
22.1 Each party shall comply with all laws applicable to its performance of this Agreement, including anti-bribery laws and the export control and economic sanctions laws of the United States.
22.2 Neither party shall export, re-export or transfer any deliverable in violation of the export control laws of the United States or of any other applicable jurisdiction.

SECTION 23. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY
23.1 Neither party is liable for any indirect, incidental, special or consequential damages, or for lost profits, even if advised of their possibility.
23.2 Except for the excluded claims below, each party's aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed one million five hundred thousand dollars ($1,500,000).
23.3 The limitation above does not apply to a party's indemnification obligations or to its breach of the confidentiality obligations in this Agreement, for which that party's aggregate liability shall not exceed seven million five hundred thousand dollars ($7,500,000).

SECTION 24. EXPENSES
24.1 Buyer shall reimburse Supplier for reasonable travel and out-of-pocket expenses that Buyer has approved in writing in advance, at cost and without mark-up, provided they comply with Buyer's travel policy as provided to Supplier.
24.2 Expense claims must be submitted within 20 days after the expense is incurred, with receipts for any single item above two hundred fifty dollars ($250).

SECTION 25. DATA PROTECTION
25.1 To the extent Supplier processes personal data on behalf of Buyer, it shall do so only on Buyer's documented instructions and in accordance with the data processing terms in Schedule D.
25.2 Supplier shall notify Buyer without undue delay, and in any event within 48 hours, after becoming aware of a security incident affecting Buyer's personal data.
25.3 Supplier shall retain Buyer's data for no longer than 90 days after the end of the applicable SOW, after which it shall securely delete that data unless retention is required by law.

SECTION 26. GOVERNING LAW
26.1 This Agreement and any dispute arising out of it are governed by the laws of the State of Colorado, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules.

SECTION 27. STATEMENTS OF WORK
27.1 The specific services, deliverables, milestones and fees for each engagement will be set out in a statement of work signed by authorized representatives of both parties (each, an "SOW"). Each SOW incorporates the terms of this Agreement.
27.2 Supplier shall not begin work under an SOW until it has been signed by both parties. Work performed before signature is at Supplier's own risk and expense.
27.3 Each SOW will identify a project manager for each party. The project managers will meet at least every 14 days to review progress, risks and open decisions.
27.4 If an SOW conflicts with this Agreement, this Agreement controls, unless the SOW expressly identifies by section number the provision of this Agreement that it overrides.

SECTION 28. AUDIT
28.1 Buyer may, on 45 days' written notice and no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, audit Supplier's records relating to fees charged under this Agreement.
28.2 Supplier shall keep those records for at least five (5) years after the fees are invoiced. If an audit shows an overcharge of more than five percent (5%), Supplier shall bear the reasonable cost of the audit.

SECTION 29. NOTICES
29.1 Notices under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered by hand, by nationally recognized overnight courier, or by email with confirmation of receipt, to the addresses set out on the signature page or as later updated by notice.
29.2 A notice is effective on receipt, or if delivered by courier, 1 Business Day(s) after dispatch.

SECTION 30. PUBLICITY
30.1 Neither party shall use the other's name or logo in any publicity, customer list or marketing material without the other's prior written consent.

SECTION 31. FORCE MAJEURE
31.1 Neither party is liable for any delay or failure to perform caused by events beyond its reasonable control, including fire, flood, war, epidemic, governmental action or failure of public utilities, provided it gives prompt notice and uses reasonable efforts to resume performance.
31.2 If a force majeure event prevents performance for more than 45 consecutive days, either party may terminate the affected SOW on written notice.

SECTION 32. PERSONNEL AND SUBCONTRACTING
32.1 Supplier shall assign Personnel with the skills and experience reasonably required to perform the Services. Supplier may replace key Personnel named in an SOW only with Buyer's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
32.2 Supplier may use subcontractors only with Buyer's prior written consent. Supplier remains responsible for the acts and omissions of its subcontractors as if they were its own.
32.3 Supplier shall ensure that its Personnel comply with Buyer's reasonable site, security and safety rules when on Buyer's premises.

SECTION 33. ENTIRE AGREEMENT AND AMENDMENT
33.1 This Agreement, including its Schedules and each SOW, is the entire agreement of the parties on its subject and supersedes all prior proposals and understandings.
33.2 This Agreement may be amended only by a written instrument signed by authorized representatives of both parties.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have caused this Agreement to be executed by their authorized representatives.

MANAGED SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Managed Services Agreement (this "Agreement") takes effect on the date on which it has been signed by both parties (the "Effective Date") by and between Stonegate Media LLC, a Texas limited liability company ("Contractor"), and Tidewater Analytics Co., a California corporation ("Company").

RECITALS. Company wishes to obtain, and Contractor wishes to provide, the services described in this Agreement on the terms set out below.

SECTION 1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Affiliate" means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a party, where "control" means ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting interests of the entity.
1.2 "Personnel" means the employees, agents and permitted subcontractors of a party who perform obligations under this Agreement.
1.3 "Documentation" means the user guides, specifications and operating manuals that Contractor makes generally available for the Services, as updated from time to time.
1.4 "Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or a day on which national banks in Dallas are authorized to close.

SECTION 2. EXPENSES
2.1 Company shall reimburse Contractor for reasonable travel and out-of-pocket expenses that Company has approved in writing in advance, at cost and without mark-up, provided they comply with Company's travel policy as provided to Contractor.
2.2 Expense claims must be submitted within 20 days after the expense is incurred, with receipts for any single item above two hundred fifty dollars ($250).

SECTION 3. ACCEPTANCE
3.1 Company shall test each deliverable against the acceptance criteria in the applicable SOW within 20 Business Days of delivery and notify Contractor in writing of acceptance or of any non-conformity.
3.2 If Company reports a non-conformity, Contractor shall correct it and redeliver within 20 days, and the acceptance procedure shall be repeated. If a deliverable fails acceptance three (3) times, Company may terminate the applicable SOW and recover the fees paid for that deliverable.

SECTION 4. INDEPENDENT CONTRACTORS
4.1 The parties are independent contractors. Nothing in this Agreement creates a partnership, joint venture, agency or employment relationship between them.

SECTION 5. VENUE
5.1 Each party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in Hennepin County, Minnesota, for any action arising out of or relating to this Agreement, and waives any objection to venue in those courts.

SECTION 6. WARRANTIES
6.1 Contractor warrants that the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with generally accepted industry standards, and that each deliverable will conform in all material respects to its specifications for 120 days after acceptance.
6.2 Company's exclusive remedy for breach of the warranty in this Section is for Contractor to re-perform the non-conforming Services or, if Contractor cannot do so within a reasonable time, a refund of the fees paid for them.
6.3 EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY STATED IN THIS AGREEMENT, NEITHER PARTY MAKES ANY OTHER WARRANTY, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING ANY IMPLIED WARRANTY OF MERCHANTABILITY OR FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.

SECTION 7. CHANGE CONTROL
7.1 Either party may request a change to the scope, schedule or fees of an SOW by written change request. Contractor shall respond within 10 Business Days with an estimate of the impact on schedule and fees.
7.2 No change is binding until a change order describing it is signed by both parties. Contractor is not obliged to perform any change until that change order is signed.

SECTION 8. NON-SOLICITATION
8.1 During the term of this Agreement and for twelve (12) months after it ends, neither party shall solicit for employment any employee of the other party who was directly involved in performing this Agreement, except through general advertisements not targeted at such employees.

SECTION 9. SEVERABILITY AND WAIVER

MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Master Services Agreement (this "Agreement") is entered into as of April 19, 2024 (the "Effective Date") by and between Copperline Security Group LLP, a New York limited liability partnership ("Contractor"), and Copperline Data Services Co., a Virginia corporation ("Company").

RECITALS. Company wishes to obtain, and Contractor wishes to provide, the services described in this Agreement on the terms set out below.

SECTION 1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or a day on which national banks in Boston are authorized to close.
1.2 "Personnel" means the employees, agents and permitted subcontractors of a party who perform obligations under this Agreement.
1.3 "Affiliate" means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a party, where "control" means ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting interests of the entity.
1.4 "Documentation" means the user guides, specifications and operating manuals that Contractor makes generally available for the Services, as updated from time to time.

SECTION 2. INDEMNIFICATION
2.1 Contractor shall defend Company against any third-party claim alleging that a deliverable infringes a patent, copyright or trademark, and pay any damages finally awarded or agreed in settlement.
2.2 The indemnified party shall give prompt notice of the claim, allow the indemnifying party to control its defense, and provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense.

SECTION 3. VENUE
3.1 Each party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in Franklin County, Ohio, for any action arising out of or relating to this Agreement, and waives any objection to venue in those courts.

SECTION 4. PUBLICITY
4.1 Neither party shall use the other's name or logo in any publicity, customer list or marketing material without the other's prior written consent.

SECTION 5. TERMINATION
5.1 Either party may terminate this Agreement or any SOW on written notice if the other party materially breaches it and fails to cure the breach within 15 days after receiving written notice describing it.
5.2 Either party may terminate this Agreement immediately on written notice if the other party becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, or has a receiver appointed for its business.
5.3 Company may terminate any SOW for convenience on 20 days' written notice, paying for Services performed up to the effective date of termination.

======================================================================

PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Professional Services Agreement (this "Agreement") is entered into as of March 18, 2023 (the "Effective Date") by and between Ashgrove Foods Corp., a Ohio corporation ("Consultant"), and Larkspur Software Inc., a Ohio corporation ("Client").

RECITALS. Client wishes to obtain, and Consultant wishes to provide, the services described in this Agreement on the terms set out below.

SECTION 1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Personnel" means the employees, agents and permitted subcontractors of a party who perform obligations under this Agreement.
1.2 "Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or a day on which national banks in Dallas are authorized to close.
1.3 "Documentation" means the user guides, specifications and operating manuals that Consultant makes generally available for the Services, as updated from time to time.
1.4 "Affiliate" means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a party, where "control" means ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting interests of the entity.

SECTION 2. NON-SOLICITATION
2.1 During the term of this Agreement and for twelve (12) months after it ends, neither party shall solicit for employment any employee of the other party who was directly involved in performing this Agreement, except through general advertisements not targeted at such employees.

SECTION 3. ACCEPTANCE
3.1 Client shall test each deliverable against the acceptance criteria in the applicable SOW within 20 Business Days of delivery and notify Consultant in writing of acceptance or of any non-conformity.
3.2 If Client reports a non-conformity, Consultant shall correct it and redeliver within 120 days, and the acceptance procedure shall be repeated. If a deliverable fails acceptance three (3) times, Client may terminate the applicable SOW and recover the fees paid for that deliverable.

SECTION 4. WARRANTIES
4.1 Consultant warrants that the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with generally accepted industry standards, and that each deliverable will conform in all material respects to its specifications for 15 days after acceptance.
4.2 Client's exclusive remedy for breach of the warranty in this Section is for Consultant to re-perform the non-conforming Services or, if Consultant cannot do so within a reasonable time, a refund of the fees paid for them.
4.3 EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY STATED IN THIS AGREEMENT, NEITHER PARTY MAKES ANY OTHER WARRANTY, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING ANY IMPLIED WARRANTY OF MERCHANTABILITY OR FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.

SECTION 5. INSURANCE
5.1 Consultant shall maintain, with insurers rated A- or better, commercial general liability insurance of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000) per occurrence, professional liability insurance of at least two million dollars ($2,000,000) per claim, and workers' compensation insurance as required by law.
5.2 Consultant shall provide certificates of insurance on request and give Client at least 45 days' notice before any required policy is cancelled or materially reduced.

SECTION 6. VENUE
6.1 Each party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in Suffolk County, Massachusetts, for any action arising out of or relating to this Agreement, and waives any objection to venue in those courts.

SECTION 7. EFFECT OF TERMINATION
7.1 On termination, Client shall pay all fees for Services performed through the effective date of termination, and each party shall return the other's Confidential Information as provided in this Agreement.
7.2 At Client's request, Consultant shall provide reasonable transition assistance for up to 90 days after termination, at the rates then in effect.

SECTION 8. FORCE MAJEURE
8.1 Neither party is liable for any delay or failure to perform caused by events beyond its reasonable control, including fire, flood, war, epidemic, governmental action or failure of public utilities, provided it gives prompt notice and uses reasonable efforts to resume performance.
8.2 If a force majeure event prevents performance for more than 120 consecutive days, either party may terminate the affected SOW on written notice.

SECTION 9. NOTICES
9.1 Notices under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered by hand, by nationally recognized overnight courier, or by email with confirmation of receipt, to the addresses set out on the signature page or as later updated by notice.
9.2 A notice is effective on receipt, or if delivered by courier, 1 Business Day(s) after dispatch.

SECTION 10. INFORMATION SECURITY
10.1 Consultant shall maintain administrative, physical and technical safeguards designed to protect Client's data, consistent with a recognized industry framework such as ISO/IEC 27001 or the NIST Cybersecurity Framework.
10.2 Consultant shall perform vulnerability scans of systems that process Client's data at least every 15 days and remediate critical findings within 45 days.

SECTION 11. DISPUTE ESCALATION
11.1 The parties shall first attempt to resolve any dispute through their project managers. If unresolved within 60 days, either party may escalate it to an executive of each party, who shall meet within a further 45 days.
11.2 Nothing in this Section prevents a party from seeking urgent injunctive relief.

SECTION 12. ASSIGNMENT
12.1 Neither party may assign this Agreement without the other party's prior written consent, except to an Affiliate or to a successor to all or substantially all of its business to which this Agreement relates, on written notice to the other party.

SECTION 13. INDEPENDENT CONTRACTORS
13.1 The parties are independent contractors. Nothing in this Agreement creates a partnership, joint venture, agency or employment relationship between them.

SECTION 14. INDEMNIFICATION
14.1 Consultant shall defend Client against any third-party claim alleging that a deliverable infringes a patent, copyright or trademark, and pay any damages finally awarded or agreed in settlement.
14.2 The indemnified party shall give prompt notice of the claim, allow the indemnifying party to control its defense, and provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense.

SECTION 15. TERMINATION
15.1 Either party may terminate this Agreement or any SOW on written notice if the other party materially breaches it and fails to cure the breach within 180 days after receiving written notice describing it.
15.2 Either party may terminate this Agreement immediately on written notice if the other party becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, or has a receiver appointed for its business.
15.3 Client may terminate any SOW for convenience on 60 days' written notice, paying for Services performed up to the effective date of termination.

SECTION 16. COUNTERPARTS
16.1 This Agreement may be signed in counterparts, including by electronic signature, each of which is an original and all of which together are one instrument.

SECTION 17. SEVERABILITY AND WAIVER
17.1 If any provision of this Agreement is held invalid, the remaining provisions remain in effect. A failure to enforce a provision is not a waiver of it.

SECTION 18. AUDIT
18.1 Client may, on 20 days' written notice and no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, audit Consultant's records relating to fees charged under this Agreement.
18.2 Consultant shall keep those records for at least three (3) years after the fees are invoiced. If an audit shows an overcharge of more than five percent (5%), Consultant shall bear the reasonable cost of the audit.

SECTION 19. TERM AND RENEWAL
19.1 The initial term of this Agreement is forty-eight (48) months from the Effective Date (the "Initial Term").
19.2 After the Initial Term, this Agreement renews automatically for successive periods of twelve (12) months each unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal at least one hundred eighty (180) days before the end of the then-current term.

SECTION 20. CHANGE CONTROL
20.1 Either party may request a change to the scope, schedule or fees of an SOW by written change request. Consultant shall respond within 5 Business Days with an estimate of the impact on schedule and fees.
20.2 No change is binding until a change order describing it is signed by both parties. Consultant is not obliged to perform any change until that change order is signed.

SECTION 21. PERSONNEL AND SUBCONTRACTING
21.1 Consultant shall assign Personnel with the skills and experience reasonably required to perform the Services. Consultant may replace key Personnel named in an SOW only with Client's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
21.2 Consultant may use subcontractors only with Client's prior written consent. Consultant remains responsible for the acts and omissions of its subcontractors as if they were its own.
21.3 Consultant shall ensure that its Personnel comply with Client's reasonable site, security and safety rules when on Client's premises.

SECTION 22. EXPENSES
22.1 Client shall reimburse Consultant for reasonable travel and out-of-pocket expenses that Client has approved in writing in advance, at cost and without mark-up, provided they comply with Client's travel policy as provided to Consultant.
22.2 Expense claims must be submitted within 120 days after the expense is incurred, with receipts for any single item above two hundred fifty dollars ($250).

SECTION 23. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY
23.1 Neither party is liable for any indirect, incidental, special or consequential damages, or for lost profits, even if advised of their possibility.
23.2 Except for the excluded claims below, each party's aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed two million five hundred thousand dollars ($2,500,000).
23.3 The limitation above does not apply to a party's indemnification obligations or to its breach of the confidentiality obligations in this Agreement, for which that party's aggregate liability shall not exceed seven million five hundred thousand dollars ($7,500,000).

SECTION 24. PUBLICITY
24.1 Neither party shall use the other's name or logo in any publicity, customer list or marketing material without the other's prior written consent.

SECTION 25. DATA PROTECTION
25.1 To the extent Consultant processes personal data on behalf of Client, it shall do so only on Client's documented instructions and in accordance with the data processing terms in Schedule D.
25.2 Consultant shall notify Client without undue delay, and in any event within 24 hours, after becoming aware of a security incident affecting Client's personal data.
25.3 Consultant shall retain Client's data for no longer than 120 days after the end of the applicable SOW, after which it shall securely delete that data unless retention is required by law.

SECTION 26. GOVERNING LAW
26.1 This Agreement and any dispute arising out of it are governed by the laws of the State of Texas, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules.

SECTION 27. CONFIDENTIALITY
27.1 Each party (the "Recipient") shall keep confidential all non-public information disclosed by the other party (the "Discloser") that is marked confidential or would reasonably be understood to be confidential ("Confidential Information"), and shall use it only to perform or receive the benefit of this Agreement.
27.2 The Recipient may disclose Confidential Information to its Personnel and professional advisers who need to know it and are bound by obligations of confidentiality no less protective than this Section.
27.3 These obligations continue for five (5) years after the expiration or termination of this Agreement, and for trade secrets for as long as they remain trade secrets under applicable law.
27.4 Within 15 days after a written request, the Recipient shall return or destroy the Discloser's Confidential Information, except for copies retained in routine backups or as required by law.

SECTION 28. STATEMENTS OF WORK
28.1 The specific services, deliverables, milestones and fees for each engagement will be set out in a statement of work signed by authorized representatives of both parties (each, an "SOW"). Each SOW incorporates the terms of this Agreement.
28.2 Consultant shall not begin work under an SOW until it has been signed by both parties. Work performed before signature is at Consultant's own risk and expense.
28.3 Each SOW will identify a project manager for each party. The project managers will meet at least every 30 days to review progress, risks and open decisions.
28.4 If an SOW conflicts with this Agreement, this Agreement controls, unless the SOW expressly identifies by section number the provision of this Agreement that it overrides.

SECTION 29. TAXES
29.1 Fees exclude sales, use, value added and similar taxes. Client shall pay any such taxes that Consultant is required to collect, other than taxes on Consultant's net income, property or employees.
29.2 If Client is required by law to withhold tax from a payment, it shall pay the amount withheld to the relevant authority and provide Consultant with evidence of payment within 10 days.

SECTION 30. ENTIRE AGREEMENT AND AMENDMENT
30.1 This Agreement, including its Schedules and each SOW, is the entire agreement of the parties on its subject and supersedes all prior proposals and understandings.
30.2 This Agreement may be amended only by a written instrument signed by authorized representatives of both parties.

SECTION 31. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY
31.1 Upon payment in full of the applicable fees, Client shall own all deliverables created specifically for Client under an SOW, and Consultant hereby assigns to Client all rights in them.
31.2 Consultant retains all rights in its pre-existing materials, tools and know-how, and in any general improvements to them. To the extent any of them is incorporated in a deliverable, Consultant grants Client a perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use it as part of that deliverable.

SECTION 32. FEES AND INVOICING
32.1 Client shall pay all undisputed amounts within 30 days after the date of Consultant's invoice. Invoices shall be issued monthly in arrears unless an SOW states otherwise.
32.2 Amounts not paid when due bear interest at the lesser of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month and the highest rate permitted by law, from the due date until paid.
32.3 Client may withhold any amount it disputes in good faith by notifying Consultant of the dispute within 45 days of the invoice date, with reasonable detail of the reasons. The parties shall work together to resolve any dispute promptly.

SECTION 33. COMPLIANCE WITH LAWS
33.1 Each party shall comply with all laws applicable to its performance of this Agreement, including anti-bribery laws and the export control and economic sanctions laws of the United States.
33.2 Neither party shall export, re-export or transfer any deliverable in violation of the export control laws of the United States or of any other applicable jurisdiction.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have caused this Agreement to be executed by their authorized representatives.
