MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Master Services Agreement (this "Agreement") is entered into as of the Effective Date by and between Lumenfield Home Goods Inc., a Minnesota corporation ("Supplier"), and Stonegate Logistics Corp., a Georgia corporation ("Buyer").

RECITALS. Buyer wishes to obtain, and Supplier wishes to provide, the services described in this Agreement on the terms set out below.

SECTION 1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Effective Date" means January 3, 2023.
1.2 "Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or a day on which national banks in Seattle are authorized to close.
1.3 "Affiliate" means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a party, where "control" means ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting interests of the entity.
1.4 "Documentation" means the user guides, specifications and operating manuals that Supplier makes generally available for the Services, as updated from time to time.
1.5 "Personnel" means the employees, agents and permitted subcontractors of a party who perform obligations under this Agreement.

SECTION 2. CHANGE CONTROL
2.1 Either party may request a change to the scope, schedule or fees of an SOW by written change request. Supplier shall respond within 5 Business Days with an estimate of the impact on schedule and fees.
2.2 No change is binding until a change order describing it is signed by both parties. Supplier is not obliged to perform any change until that change order is signed.

SECTION 3. AUDIT
3.1 Buyer may, on 30 days' written notice and no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, audit Supplier's records relating to fees charged under this Agreement.
3.2 Supplier shall keep those records for at least three (3) years after the fees are invoiced. If an audit shows an overcharge of more than five percent (5%), Supplier shall bear the reasonable cost of the audit.

SECTION 4. FEES AND INVOICING
4.1 Buyer shall pay all undisputed amounts within 90 days after the date of Supplier's invoice. Invoices shall be issued monthly in arrears unless an SOW states otherwise.
4.2 Amounts not paid when due bear interest at the lesser of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month and the highest rate permitted by law, from the due date until paid.
4.3 Buyer may withhold any amount it disputes in good faith by notifying Supplier of the dispute within 120 days of the invoice date, with reasonable detail of the reasons. The parties shall work together to resolve any dispute promptly.

SECTION 5. TERMINATION
5.1 Either party may terminate this Agreement or any SOW on written notice if the other party materially breaches it and fails to cure the breach within 30 days after receiving written notice describing it.
5.2 Either party may terminate this Agreement immediately on written notice if the other party becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, or has a receiver appointed for its business.
5.3 Buyer may terminate any SOW for convenience on 15 days' written notice, paying for Services performed up to the effective date of termination.

SECTION 6. CONFIDENTIALITY
6.1 Each party (the "Recipient") shall keep confidential all non-public information disclosed by the other party (the "Discloser") that is marked confidential or would reasonably be understood to be confidential ("Confidential Information"), and shall use it only to perform or receive the benefit of this Agreement.
6.2 The Recipient may disclose Confidential Information to its Personnel and professional advisers who need to know it and are bound by obligations of confidentiality no less protective than this Section.
6.3 These obligations continue for two (2) years after the expiration or termination of this Agreement, and for trade secrets for as long as they remain trade secrets under applicable law.
6.4 Within 30 days after a written request, the Recipient shall return or destroy the Discloser's Confidential Information, except for copies retained in routine backups or as required by law.

SECTION 7. NOTICES
7.1 Notices under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered by hand, by nationally recognized overnight courier, or by email with confirmation of receipt, to the addresses set out on the signature page or as later updated by notice.
7.2 A notice is effective on receipt, or if delivered by courier, 2 Business Day(s) after dispatch.

SECTION 8. WARRANTIES
8.1 Supplier warrants that the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with generally accepted industry standards, and that each deliverable will conform in all material respects to its specifications for 45 days after acceptance.
8.2 Buyer's exclusive remedy for breach of the warranty in this Section is for Supplier to re-perform the non-conforming Services or, if Supplier cannot do so within a reasonable time, a refund of the fees paid for them.
8.3 EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY STATED IN THIS AGREEMENT, NEITHER PARTY MAKES ANY OTHER WARRANTY, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING ANY IMPLIED WARRANTY OF MERCHANTABILITY OR FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.

SECTION 9. EFFECT OF TERMINATION
9.1 On termination, Buyer shall pay all fees for Services performed through the effective date of termination, and each party shall return the other's Confidential Information as provided in this Agreement.
9.2 At Buyer's request, Supplier shall provide reasonable transition assistance for up to 15 days after termination, at the rates then in effect.

SECTION 10. TAXES
10.1 Fees exclude sales, use, value added and similar taxes. Buyer shall pay any such taxes that Supplier is required to collect, other than taxes on Supplier's net income, property or employees.
10.2 If Buyer is required by law to withhold tax from a payment, it shall pay the amount withheld to the relevant authority and provide Supplier with evidence of payment within 120 days.

SECTION 11. INDEPENDENT CONTRACTORS
11.1 The parties are independent contractors. Nothing in this Agreement creates a partnership, joint venture, agency or employment relationship between them.

SECTION 12. DISPUTE ESCALATION
12.1 The parties shall first attempt to resolve any dispute through their project managers. If unresolved within 20 days, either party may escalate it to an executive of each party, who shall meet within a further 10 days.
12.2 Nothing in this Section prevents a party from seeking urgent injunctive relief.

SECTION 13. DATA PROTECTION
13.1 To the extent Supplier processes personal data on behalf of Buyer, it shall do so only on Buyer's documented instructions and in accordance with the data processing terms in Schedule D.
13.2 Supplier shall notify Buyer without undue delay, and in any event within 48 hours, after becoming aware of a security incident affecting Buyer's personal data.
13.3 Supplier shall retain Buyer's data for no longer than 180 days after the end of the applicable SOW, after which it shall securely delete that data unless retention is required by law.

SECTION 14. SEVERABILITY AND WAIVER
14.1 If any provision of this Agreement is held invalid, the remaining provisions remain in effect. A failure to enforce a provision is not a waiver of it.

SECTION 15. FORCE MAJEURE
15.1 Neither party is liable for any delay or failure to perform caused by events beyond its reasonable control, including fire, flood, war, epidemic, governmental action or failure of public utilities, provided it gives prompt notice and uses reasonable efforts to resume performance.
15.2 If a force majeure event prevents performance for more than 60 consecutive days, either party may terminate the affected SOW on written notice.

SECTION 16. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY
16.1 Upon payment in full of the applicable fees, Buyer shall own all deliverables created specifically for Buyer under an SOW, and Supplier hereby assigns to Buyer all rights in them.
16.2 Supplier retains all rights in its pre-existing materials, tools and know-how, and in any general improvements to them. To the extent any of them is incorporated in a deliverable, Supplier grants Buyer a perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use it as part of that deliverable.

SECTION 17. COUNTERPARTS
17.1 This Agreement may be signed in counterparts, including by electronic signature, each of which is an original and all of which together are one instrument.

SECTION 18. ENTIRE AGREEMENT AND AMENDMENT
18.1 This Agreement, including its Schedules and each SOW, is the entire agreement of the parties on its subject and supersedes all prior proposals and understandings.
18.2 This Agreement may be amended only by a written instrument signed by authorized representatives of both parties.

SECTION 19. TERM AND RENEWAL
19.1 The initial term of this Agreement is sixty (60) months from the Effective Date (the "Initial Term").
19.2 The parties may renew this Agreement for additional periods of twelve (12) months each by mutual written agreement signed at least ninety (90) days before the end of the then-current term. Absent such agreement, this Agreement expires at the end of the then-current term.

SECTION 20. PERSONNEL AND SUBCONTRACTING
20.1 Supplier shall assign Personnel with the skills and experience reasonably required to perform the Services. Supplier may replace key Personnel named in an SOW only with Buyer's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
20.2 Supplier may use subcontractors only with Buyer's prior written consent. Supplier remains responsible for the acts and omissions of its subcontractors as if they were its own.
20.3 Supplier shall ensure that its Personnel comply with Buyer's reasonable site, security and safety rules when on Buyer's premises.

SECTION 21. VENUE
21.1 Each party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in Franklin County, Ohio, for any action arising out of or relating to this Agreement, and waives any objection to venue in those courts.

SECTION 22. INSURANCE
22.1 Supplier shall maintain, with insurers rated A- or better, commercial general liability insurance of at least three million dollars ($3,000,000) per occurrence, professional liability insurance of at least three million dollars ($3,000,000) per claim, and workers' compensation insurance as required by law.
22.2 Supplier shall provide certificates of insurance on request and give Buyer at least 20 days' notice before any required policy is cancelled or materially reduced.

SECTION 23. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY
23.1 Neither party is liable for any indirect, incidental, special or consequential damages, or for lost profits, even if advised of their possibility.
23.2 Except for the excluded claims below, each party's aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the fees paid or payable by Buyer under this Agreement in the six (6) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.
23.3 The limitation above does not apply to a party's indemnification obligations or to its breach of the confidentiality obligations in this Agreement, for which that party's aggregate liability shall not exceed ten million dollars ($10,000,000).

SECTION 24. COMPLIANCE WITH LAWS
24.1 Each party shall comply with all laws applicable to its performance of this Agreement, including anti-bribery laws and the export control and economic sanctions laws of the United States.
24.2 Neither party shall export, re-export or transfer any deliverable in violation of the export control laws of the United States or of any other applicable jurisdiction.

SECTION 25. EXPENSES
25.1 Buyer shall reimburse Supplier for reasonable travel and out-of-pocket expenses that Buyer has approved in writing in advance, at cost and without mark-up, provided they comply with Buyer's travel policy as provided to Supplier.
25.2 Expense claims must be submitted within 20 days after the expense is incurred, with receipts for any single item above two hundred fifty dollars ($250).

SECTION 26. GOVERNING LAW
26.1 This Agreement and any dispute arising out of it are governed by the laws of the State of Ohio, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules.

SECTION 27. PUBLICITY

MANAGED SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Managed Services Agreement (this "Agreement") is entered into as of August 2, 2023 (the "Effective Date") by and between Brightwater Energy Holdings, Inc., a Oregon corporation ("Vendor"), and Ironleaf Freight Co., a Florida corporation ("Client").

RECITALS. Client wishes to obtain, and Vendor wishes to provide, the services described in this Agreement on the terms set out below.

SECTION 1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Documentation" means the user guides, specifications and operating manuals that Vendor makes generally available for the Services, as updated from time to time.
1.2 "Affiliate" means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a party, where "control" means ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting interests of the entity.
1.3 "Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or a day on which national banks in Atlanta are authorized to close.
1.4 "Personnel" means the employees, agents and permitted subcontractors of a party who perform obligations under this Agreement.

SECTION 2. DATA PROTECTION
2.1 To the extent Vendor processes personal data on behalf of Client, it shall do so only on Client's documented instructions and in accordance with the data processing terms in Schedule D.
2.2 Vendor shall notify Client without undue delay, and in any event within 24 hours, after becoming aware of a security incident affecting Client's personal data.
2.3 Vendor shall retain Client's data for no longer than 30 days after the end of the applicable SOW, after which it shall securely delete that data unless retention is required by law.

SECTION 3. CONFIDENTIALITY
3.1 Each party (the "Recipient") shall keep confidential all non-public information disclosed by the other party (the "Discloser") that is marked confidential or would reasonably be understood to be confidential ("Confidential Information"), and shall use it only to perform or receive the benefit of this Agreement.
3.2 The Recipient may disclose Confidential Information to its Personnel and professional advisers who need to know it and are bound by obligations of confidentiality no less protective than this Section.
3.3 These obligations continue for two (2) years after the expiration or termination of this Agreement, and for trade secrets for as long as they remain trade secrets under applicable law.
3.4 Within 10 days after a written request, the Recipient shall return or destroy the Discloser's Confidential Information, except for copies retained in routine backups or as required by law.

SECTION 4. INDEPENDENT CONTRACTORS
4.1 The parties are independent contractors. Nothing in this Agreement creates a partnership, joint venture, agency or employment relationship between them.

SECTION 5. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

SOFTWARE SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Software Services Agreement (this "Agreement") is entered into as of November 19, 2024 (the "Effective Date") by and between Sablewood Security Group LLC, a Washington limited liability company ("Provider"), and Quillstone Media LLC, a Texas limited liability company ("Customer").

RECITALS. Customer wishes to obtain, and Provider wishes to provide, the services described in this Agreement on the terms set out below.

SECTION 1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Documentation" means the user guides, specifications and operating manuals that Provider makes generally available for the Services, as updated from time to time.
1.2 "Personnel" means the employees, agents and permitted subcontractors of a party who perform obligations under this Agreement.
1.3 "Affiliate" means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a party, where "control" means ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting interests of the entity.
1.4 "Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or a day on which national banks in Minneapolis are authorized to close.

SECTION 2. TAXES
2.1 Fees exclude sales, use, value added and similar taxes. Customer shall pay any such taxes that Provider is required to collect, other than taxes on Provider's net income, property or employees.
2.2 If Customer is required by law to withhold tax from a payment, it shall pay the amount withheld to the relevant authority and provide Provider with evidence of payment within 30 days.

SECTION 3. DATA PROTECTION
3.1 To the extent Provider processes personal data on behalf of Customer, it shall do so only on Customer's documented instructions and in accordance with the data processing terms in Schedule D.
3.2 Provider shall notify Customer without undue delay, and in any event within 48 hours, after becoming aware of a security incident affecting Customer's personal data.

MANAGED SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Managed Services Agreement (this "Agreement") takes effect on the date on which it has been signed by both parties (the "Effective Date") by and between Stonegate Energy Co., a Minnesota corporation ("Provider"), and Kitebridge Energy LLP, a Washington limited liability partnership ("Customer").

RECITALS. Customer wishes to obtain, and Provider wishes to provide, the services described in this Agreement on the terms set out below.

SECTION 1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Documentation" means the user guides, specifications and operating manuals that Provider makes generally available for the Services, as updated from time to time.
1.2 "Personnel" means the employees, agents and permitted subcontractors of a party who perform obligations under this Agreement.
1.3 "Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or a day on which national banks in Dallas are authorized to close.
1.4 "Affiliate" means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a party, where "control" means ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting interests of the entity.

SECTION 2. WARRANTIES
2.1 Provider warrants that the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with generally accepted industry standards, and that each deliverable will conform in all material respects to its specifications for 90 days after acceptance.
2.2 Customer's exclusive remedy for breach of the warranty in this Section is for Provider to re-perform the non-conforming Services or, if Provider cannot do so within a reasonable time, a refund of the fees paid for them.
2.3 EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY STATED IN THIS AGREEMENT, NEITHER PARTY MAKES ANY OTHER WARRANTY, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING ANY IMPLIED WARRANTY OF MERCHANTABILITY OR FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.

SECTION 3. FORCE MAJEURE
3.1 Neither party is liable for any delay or failure to perform caused by events beyond its reasonable control, including fire, flood, war, epidemic, governmental action or failure of public utilities, provided it gives prompt notice and uses reasonable efforts to resume performance.
3.2 If a force majeure event prevents performance for more than 90 consecutive days, either party may terminate the affected SOW on written notice.

SECTION 4. CHANGE CONTROL
4.1 Either party may request a change to the scope, schedule or fees of an SOW by written change request. Provider shall respond within 10 Business Days with an estimate of the impact on schedule and fees.
4.2 No change is binding until a change order describing it is signed by both parties. Provider is not obliged to perform any change until that change order is signed.

SECTION 5. NON-SOLICITATION

======================================================================

TECHNOLOGY SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Technology Services Agreement (this "Agreement") is entered into as of July 21, 2023 (the "Effective Date") by and between Ashgrove Supply LLC, a Washington limited liability company ("Consultant"), and Silverbirch Health Partners Holdings, Inc., a Georgia corporation ("Client").

RECITALS. Client wishes to obtain, and Consultant wishes to provide, the services described in this Agreement on the terms set out below.

SECTION 1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Affiliate" means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a party, where "control" means ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting interests of the entity.
1.2 "Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or a day on which national banks in Boston are authorized to close.
1.3 "Documentation" means the user guides, specifications and operating manuals that Consultant makes generally available for the Services, as updated from time to time.
1.4 "Personnel" means the employees, agents and permitted subcontractors of a party who perform obligations under this Agreement.

SECTION 2. CHANGE CONTROL
2.1 Either party may request a change to the scope, schedule or fees of an SOW by written change request. Consultant shall respond within 5 Business Days with an estimate of the impact on schedule and fees.
2.2 No change is binding until a change order describing it is signed by both parties. Consultant is not obliged to perform any change until that change order is signed.

SECTION 3. PERSONNEL AND SUBCONTRACTING
3.1 Consultant shall assign Personnel with the skills and experience reasonably required to perform the Services. Consultant may replace key Personnel named in an SOW only with Client's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
3.2 Consultant may use subcontractors only with Client's prior written consent. Consultant remains responsible for the acts and omissions of its subcontractors as if they were its own.
3.3 Consultant shall ensure that its Personnel comply with Client's reasonable site, security and safety rules when on Client's premises.

SECTION 4. ASSIGNMENT
4.1 Neither party may assign this Agreement without the other party's prior written consent, except to an Affiliate or to a successor to all or substantially all of its business to which this Agreement relates, on written notice to the other party.

SECTION 5. ENTIRE AGREEMENT AND AMENDMENT
5.1 This Agreement, including its Schedules and each SOW, is the entire agreement of the parties on its subject and supersedes all prior proposals and understandings.
5.2 This Agreement may be amended only by a written instrument signed by authorized representatives of both parties.

SECTION 6. INDEMNIFICATION
6.1 Consultant shall defend Client against any third-party claim alleging that a deliverable infringes a patent, copyright or trademark, and pay any damages finally awarded or agreed in settlement.
6.2 The indemnified party shall give prompt notice of the claim, allow the indemnifying party to control its defense, and provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense.

SECTION 7. STATEMENTS OF WORK
7.1 The specific services, deliverables, milestones and fees for each engagement will be set out in a statement of work signed by authorized representatives of both parties (each, an "SOW"). Each SOW incorporates the terms of this Agreement.
7.2 Consultant shall not begin work under an SOW until it has been signed by both parties. Work performed before signature is at Consultant's own risk and expense.
7.3 Each SOW will identify a project manager for each party. The project managers will meet at least every 30 days to review progress, risks and open decisions.
7.4 If an SOW conflicts with this Agreement, this Agreement controls, unless the SOW expressly identifies by section number the provision of this Agreement that it overrides.

SECTION 8. EFFECT OF TERMINATION
8.1 On termination, Client shall pay all fees for Services performed through the effective date of termination, and each party shall return the other's Confidential Information as provided in this Agreement.
8.2 At Client's request, Consultant shall provide reasonable transition assistance for up to 90 days after termination, at the rates then in effect.

SECTION 9. WARRANTIES
9.1 Consultant warrants that the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with generally accepted industry standards, and that each deliverable will conform in all material respects to its specifications for 45 days after acceptance.
9.2 Client's exclusive remedy for breach of the warranty in this Section is for Consultant to re-perform the non-conforming Services or, if Consultant cannot do so within a reasonable time, a refund of the fees paid for them.
9.3 EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY STATED IN THIS AGREEMENT, NEITHER PARTY MAKES ANY OTHER WARRANTY, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING ANY IMPLIED WARRANTY OF MERCHANTABILITY OR FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.

SECTION 10. DISPUTE ESCALATION
10.1 The parties shall first attempt to resolve any dispute through their project managers. If unresolved within 30 days, either party may escalate it to an executive of each party, who shall meet within a further 15 days.
10.2 Nothing in this Section prevents a party from seeking urgent injunctive relief.

SECTION 11. COUNTERPARTS
11.1 This Agreement may be signed in counterparts, including by electronic signature, each of which is an original and all of which together are one instrument.

SECTION 12. INDEPENDENT CONTRACTORS
12.1 The parties are independent contractors. Nothing in this Agreement creates a partnership, joint venture, agency or employment relationship between them.

SECTION 13. PUBLICITY
13.1 Neither party shall use the other's name or logo in any publicity, customer list or marketing material without the other's prior written consent.

SECTION 14. COMPLIANCE WITH LAWS
14.1 Each party shall comply with all laws applicable to its performance of this Agreement, including anti-bribery laws and the export control and economic sanctions laws of the United States.
14.2 Neither party shall export, re-export or transfer any deliverable in violation of the export control laws of the United States or of any other applicable jurisdiction.

SECTION 15. NOTICES
15.1 Notices under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered by hand, by nationally recognized overnight courier, or by email with confirmation of receipt, to the addresses set out on the signature page or as later updated by notice.
15.2 A notice is effective on receipt, or if delivered by courier, 2 Business Day(s) after dispatch.

SECTION 16. TERMINATION
16.1 Either party may terminate this Agreement or any SOW on written notice if the other party materially breaches it and fails to cure the breach within 15 days after receiving written notice describing it.
16.2 Either party may terminate this Agreement immediately on written notice if the other party becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, or has a receiver appointed for its business.
16.3 Client may terminate any SOW for convenience on 180 days' written notice, paying for Services performed up to the effective date of termination.

SECTION 17. SEVERABILITY AND WAIVER
17.1 If any provision of this Agreement is held invalid, the remaining provisions remain in effect. A failure to enforce a provision is not a waiver of it.

SECTION 18. EXPENSES
18.1 Client shall reimburse Consultant for reasonable travel and out-of-pocket expenses that Client has approved in writing in advance, at cost and without mark-up, provided they comply with Client's travel policy as provided to Consultant.
18.2 Expense claims must be submitted within 180 days after the expense is incurred, with receipts for any single item above two hundred fifty dollars ($250).

SECTION 19. TERM AND RENEWAL
19.1 The initial term of this Agreement begins on the Effective Date and ends on January 20, 2025 (the "Initial Term").
19.2 After the Initial Term, this Agreement renews automatically for successive periods of twenty-four (24) months each unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal at least forty-five (45) days before the end of the then-current term.

SECTION 20. AUDIT
20.1 Client may, on 180 days' written notice and no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, audit Consultant's records relating to fees charged under this Agreement.
20.2 Consultant shall keep those records for at least five (5) years after the fees are invoiced. If an audit shows an overcharge of more than five percent (5%), Consultant shall bear the reasonable cost of the audit.

SECTION 21. INSURANCE
21.1 Consultant shall maintain, with insurers rated A- or better, commercial general liability insurance of at least two million dollars ($2,000,000) per occurrence, professional liability insurance of at least two million dollars ($2,000,000) per claim, and workers' compensation insurance as required by law.
21.2 Consultant shall provide certificates of insurance on request and give Client at least 45 days' notice before any required policy is cancelled or materially reduced.

SECTION 22. FORCE MAJEURE
22.1 Neither party is liable for any delay or failure to perform caused by events beyond its reasonable control, including fire, flood, war, epidemic, governmental action or failure of public utilities, provided it gives prompt notice and uses reasonable efforts to resume performance.
22.2 If a force majeure event prevents performance for more than 10 consecutive days, either party may terminate the affected SOW on written notice.

SECTION 23. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY
23.1 Neither party is liable for any indirect, incidental, special or consequential damages, or for lost profits, even if advised of their possibility.
23.2 Except for the excluded claims below, each party's aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) five hundred thousand dollars ($500,000) and (b) the fees paid or payable by Client under this Agreement in the twenty-four (24) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.
23.3 The limitation above does not apply to a party's indemnification obligations or to its breach of the confidentiality obligations in this Agreement, for which that party's aggregate liability shall not exceed seven million five hundred thousand dollars ($7,500,000).

SECTION 24. TAXES
24.1 Fees exclude sales, use, value added and similar taxes. Client shall pay any such taxes that Consultant is required to collect, other than taxes on Consultant's net income, property or employees.
24.2 If Client is required by law to withhold tax from a payment, it shall pay the amount withheld to the relevant authority and provide Consultant with evidence of payment within 20 days.

SECTION 25. VENUE
25.1 Each party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in Suffolk County, Massachusetts, for any action arising out of or relating to this Agreement, and waives any objection to venue in those courts.

SECTION 26. GOVERNING LAW
26.1 This Agreement and any dispute arising out of it are governed by the laws of the State of Washington, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules.

SECTION 27. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY
27.1 Upon payment in full of the applicable fees, Client shall own all deliverables created specifically for Client under an SOW, and Consultant hereby assigns to Client all rights in them.
27.2 Consultant retains all rights in its pre-existing materials, tools and know-how, and in any general improvements to them. To the extent any of them is incorporated in a deliverable, Consultant grants Client a perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use it as part of that deliverable.

SECTION 28. CONFIDENTIALITY
28.1 Each party (the "Recipient") shall keep confidential all non-public information disclosed by the other party (the "Discloser") that is marked confidential or would reasonably be understood to be confidential ("Confidential Information"), and shall use it only to perform or receive the benefit of this Agreement.
28.2 The Recipient may disclose Confidential Information to its Personnel and professional advisers who need to know it and are bound by obligations of confidentiality no less protective than this Section.
28.3 These obligations continue for five (5) years after the expiration or termination of this Agreement, and for trade secrets for as long as they remain trade secrets under applicable law.
28.4 Within 20 days after a written request, the Recipient shall return or destroy the Discloser's Confidential Information, except for copies retained in routine backups or as required by law.

SECTION 29. NON-SOLICITATION
29.1 During the term of this Agreement and for eighteen (18) months after it ends, neither party shall solicit for employment any employee of the other party who was directly involved in performing this Agreement, except through general advertisements not targeted at such employees.

SECTION 30. INFORMATION SECURITY
30.1 Consultant shall maintain administrative, physical and technical safeguards designed to protect Client's data, consistent with a recognized industry framework such as ISO/IEC 27001 or the NIST Cybersecurity Framework.
30.2 Consultant shall perform vulnerability scans of systems that process Client's data at least every 120 days and remediate critical findings within 60 days.

SECTION 31. DATA PROTECTION
31.1 To the extent Consultant processes personal data on behalf of Client, it shall do so only on Client's documented instructions and in accordance with the data processing terms in Schedule D.
31.2 Consultant shall notify Client without undue delay, and in any event within 48 hours, after becoming aware of a security incident affecting Client's personal data.
31.3 Consultant shall retain Client's data for no longer than 180 days after the end of the applicable SOW, after which it shall securely delete that data unless retention is required by law.

SECTION 32. ACCEPTANCE
32.1 Client shall test each deliverable against the acceptance criteria in the applicable SOW within 10 Business Days of delivery and notify Consultant in writing of acceptance or of any non-conformity.
32.2 If Client reports a non-conformity, Consultant shall correct it and redeliver within 30 days, and the acceptance procedure shall be repeated. If a deliverable fails acceptance three (3) times, Client may terminate the applicable SOW and recover the fees paid for that deliverable.

SECTION 33. FEES AND INVOICING
33.1 Client shall pay all undisputed amounts within 45 days after the date of Consultant's invoice. Invoices shall be issued monthly in arrears unless an SOW states otherwise.
33.2 Amounts not paid when due bear interest at the lesser of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month and the highest rate permitted by law, from the due date until paid.
33.3 Client may withhold any amount it disputes in good faith by notifying Consultant of the dispute within 45 days of the invoice date, with reasonable detail of the reasons. The parties shall work together to resolve any dispute promptly.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have caused this Agreement to be executed by their authorized representatives.

This Professional Services Agreement (this "Agreement") takes effect on the
date on which it has been signed by botb parties (the "Effective Date") by and
between Kitebridge Health Partners Inc., a Ohio corporation ("Consultant"),
and Granite Peak Lab Services Corp., a Delaware corporation ("Client").

RECITALS. Client wishes to obtain, and Consultant wishes to provide, the serv-
ices described in this Agreement on the terms set out below.

SECTION 1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or a day on
which national banks in Seattle are authorized to close.
1.2 "Documentation" means the user guides, specifications and operating
manuals that Consultant makes generally available for the Services, as updated
from time to time.
1.3 "Personnel" means the employees, agents and permitted subcontractors of a
party who perform obligations under this Agreement.
1.4 "Affiliate" means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is
controlled by, or is under common control with a party, where "control" means
ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting interests of the
entity.

SECTION 2. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY
2.1 Upon payment in full of the applicable fees, Client shall own all
deliverables created specifically for Client under an SOW, and Consultant her-
eby assigns to Client all rights in them.
2.2 Consultant retains all rights in its pre-existing materials, tools and
know-how, and in any general improvements to them. To the extent any of them
is incorporated in a deliverable, Consultant grants Client a perpetual,
non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use it as part of that deliverable.

SECTION 3. AUDIT
3.1 Client may, on 30 days' written notice and no more than once in any twelve
(12) month period, audit Consultant's records relating to fees charged under
this Agreement.
3.2 Consultant shall keep those records for at least three (3) years after the
fees are invoiced. If an audit shows an overcharge of more than five percent
(5%), Consultant shall bear the reasonable cost of the audit.

SECTION 4. DATA PROTECTION
4.1 To the extent Consultant processes personal data on behalf of Client, it
shall do so only on Client's documented instructions and in accordance with
the data processing terms in Schedule D.
4.2 Consultant shall notify Client without undue delay, and in any event
within 24 hours, after becoming aware of a security incident affecting
Client's personal data.
4.3 Consultant shall retain Client's data for no longer than 30 days after the

unless retention is required by law.

finally awarded or agreed in settlement.
5.2 The indemnified party shall give prompt notice of the claim, allow the
indemnifying party to control its defense, and provide reasonable cooperation
at the indemnifying party's expense.

SECTION 6. ASSIGNMENT
6.1 Neither party may assign this Agreement without the other party's prior
written consent, except to an Affiliate or to a successor to all or
substantially all of its business to which this Agreement relates, on written
notice to the other party.

7.1 Neither party is liable for any delay or failure to perform caused by
events beyond its reasonable control, including fire, flood, war, epidemic,
governmental action or failure of public utilities, provided it gives prompt

days, either party may terminate the affected SOW on written notice.

ions remain in effect. A failure to enforce a provision is not a waiver of it.

SOFTWARE SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Software Services Agreement (this "Agreement") takes effect on the date on which it has been signed by both parties (the "Effective Date") by and between Corvane Lab Services LLP, a New York limited liability partnership ("Consultant"), and Brookhaven Systems Holdings, Inc., a Massachusetts corporation ("Client").

RECITALS. Client wishes to obtain, and Consultant wishes to provide, the services described in this Agreement on the terms set out below.

SECTION 1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Affiliate" means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a party, where "control" means ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting interests of the entity.
1.2 "Documentation" means the user guides, specifications and operating manuals that Consultant makes generally available for the Services, as updated from time to time.
1.3 "Personnel" means the employees, agents and permitted subcontractors of a party who perform obligations under this Agreement.
1.4 "Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or a day on which national banks in Dallas are authorized to close.

SECTION 2. PUBLICITY
2.1 Neither party shall use the other's name or logo in any publicity, customer list or marketing material without the other's prior written consent.

SECTION 3. ACCEPTANCE
3.1 Client shall test each deliverable against the acceptance criteria in the applicable SOW within 15 Business Days of delivery and notify Consultant in writing of acceptance or of any non-conformity.
3.2 If Client reports a non-conformity, Consultant shall correct it and redeliver within 120 days, and the acceptance procedure shall be repeated. If a deliverable fails acceptance three (3) times, Client may terminate the applicable SOW and recover the fees paid for that deliverable.

SECTION 4. COUNTERPARTS
4.1 This Agreement may be signed in counterparts, including by electronic signature, each of which is an original and all of which together are one instrument.

SECTION 5. AUDIT
5.1 Client may, on 10 days' written notice and no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, audit Consultant's records relating to fees charged under this Agreement.
5.2 Consultant shall keep those records for at least seven (7) years after the fees are invoiced. If an audit shows an overcharge of more than five percent (5%), Consultant shall bear the reasonable cost of the audit.

SECTION 6. EXPENSES
6.1 Client shall reimburse Consultant for reasonable travel and out-of-pocket expenses that Client has approved in writing in advance, at cost and without mark-up, provided they comply with Client's travel policy as provided to Consultant.
6.2 Expense claims must be submitted within 60 days after the expense is incurred, with receipts for any single item above two hundred fifty dollars ($250).

SECTION 7. CHANGE CONTROL
7.1 Either party may request a change to the scope, schedule or fees of an SOW by written change request. Consultant shall respond within 10 Business Days with an estimate of the impact on schedule and fees.
7.2 No change is binding until a change order describing it is signed by both parties. Consultant is not obliged to perform any change until that change order is signed.

SECTION 8. EFFECT OF TERMINATION
8.1 On termination, Client shall pay all fees for Services performed through the effective date of termination, and each party shall return the other's Confidential Information as provided in this Agreement.
8.2 At Client's request, Consultant shall provide reasonable transition assistance for up to 30 days after termination, at the rates then in effect.

SECTION 9. SEVERABILITY AND WAIVER
9.1 If any provision of this Agreement is held invalid, the remaining provisions remain in effect. A failure to enforce a provision is not a waiver of it.

SECTION 10. NOTICES
10.1 Notices under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered by hand, by nationally recognized overnight courier, or by email with confirmation of receipt, to the addresses set out on the signature page or as later updated by notice.
10.2 A notice is effective on receipt, or if delivered by courier, 1 Business Day(s) after dispatch.

SECTION 11. INDEMNIFICATION
11.1 Consultant shall defend Client against any third-party claim alleging that a deliverable infringes a patent, copyright or trademark, and pay any damages finally awarded or agreed in settlement.
11.2 The indemnified party shall give prompt notice of the claim, allow the indemnifying party to control its defense, and provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense.

SECTION 12. INFORMATION SECURITY
12.1 Consultant shall maintain administrative, physical and technical safeguards designed to protect Client's data, consistent with a recognized industry framework such as ISO/IEC 27001 or the NIST Cybersecurity Framework.
12.2 Consultant shall perform vulnerability scans of systems that process Client's data at least every 90 days and remediate critical findings within 30 days.

SECTION 13. ASSIGNMENT
13.1 Neither party may assign this Agreement without the other party's prior written consent, except to an Affiliate or to a successor to all or substantially all of its business to which this Agreement relates, on written notice to the other party.

SECTION 14. NON-SOLICITATION
14.1 During the term of this Agreement and for twelve (12) months after it ends, neither party shall solicit for employment any employee of the other party who was directly involved in performing this Agreement, except through general advertisements not targeted at such employees.

SECTION 15. VENUE
15.1 Each party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New Castle County, Delaware, for any action arising out of or relating to this Agreement, and waives any objection to venue in those courts.

SECTION 16. TERMINATION
16.1 Either party may terminate this Agreement or any SOW on written notice if the other party materially breaches it and fails to cure the breach within 120 days after receiving written notice describing it.
16.2 Either party may terminate this Agreement immediately on written notice if the other party becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, or has a receiver appointed for its business.
16.3 Client may terminate any SOW for convenience on 15 days' written notice, paying for Services performed up to the effective date of termination.

SECTION 17. CONFIDENTIALITY
17.1 Each party (the "Recipient") shall keep confidential all non-public information disclosed by the other party (the "Discloser") that is marked confidential or would reasonably be understood to be confidential ("Confidential Information"), and shall use it only to perform or receive the benefit of this Agreement.
17.2 The Recipient may disclose Confidential Information to its Personnel and professional advisers who need to know it and are bound by obligations of confidentiality no less protective than this Section.
17.3 These obligations continue for two (2) years after the expiration or termination of this Agreement, and for trade secrets for as long as they remain trade secrets under applicable law.

MANAGED SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Managed Services Agreement (this "Agreement") is entered into as of the Effective Date by and between Granite Peak Manufacturing LLP, a Virginia limited liability partnership ("Supplier"), and Cobalt Ridge Foods LLC, a New York limited liability company ("Buyer").

RECITALS. Buyer wishes to obtain, and Supplier wishes to provide, the services described in this Agreement on the terms set out below.

SECTION 1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Personnel" means the employees, agents and permitted subcontractors of a party who perform obligations under this Agreement.
1.2 "Documentation" means the user guides, specifications and operating manuals that Supplier makes generally available for the Services, as updated from time to time.
1.3 "Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or a day on which national banks in Seattle are authorized to close.
1.4 "Affiliate" means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a party, where "control" means ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting interests of the entity.
1.5 "Effective Date" means November 5, 2023.

SECTION 2. PUBLICITY
2.1 Neither party shall use the other's name or logo in any publicity, customer list or marketing material without the other's prior written consent.

SECTION 3. CHANGE CONTROL
3.1 Either party may request a change to the scope, schedule or fees of an SOW by written change request. Supplier shall respond within 5 Business Days with an estimate of the impact on schedule and fees.
3.2 No change is binding until a change order describing it is signed by both parties. Supplier is not obliged to perform any change until that change order is signed.

SECTION 4. INSURANCE
4.1 Supplier shall maintain, with insurers rated A- or better, commercial general liability insurance of at least two million dollars ($2,000,000) per occurrence, professional liability insurance of at least three million dollars ($3,000,000) per claim, and workers' compensation insurance as required by law.
4.2 Supplier shall provide certificates of insurance on request and give Buyer at least 30 days' notice before any required policy is cancelled or materially reduced.

SECTION 5. ASSIGNMENT
5.1 Neither party may assign this Agreement without the other party's prior written consent, except to an Affiliate or to a successor to all or substantially all of its business to which this Agreement relates, on written notice to the other party.

SECTION 6. AUDIT
6.1 Buyer may, on 90 days' written notice and no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, audit Supplier's records relating to fees charged under this Agreement.
6.2 Supplier shall keep those records for at least three (3) years after the fees are invoiced. If an audit shows an overcharge of more than five percent (5%), Supplier shall bear the reasonable cost of the audit.

SECTION 7. SEVERABILITY AND WAIVER
7.1 If any provision of this Agreement is held invalid, the remaining provisions remain in effect. A failure to enforce a provision is not a waiver of it.

SECTION 8. NON-SOLICITATION
8.1 During the term of this Agreement and for six (6) months after it ends, neither party shall solicit for employment any employee of the other party who was directly involved in performing this Agreement, except through general advertisements not targeted at such employees.

SECTION 9. NOTICES
9.1 Notices under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered by hand, by nationally recognized overnight courier, or by email with confirmation of receipt, to the addresses set out on the signature page or as later updated by notice.
9.2 A notice is effective on receipt, or if delivered by courier, 1 Business Day(s) after dispatch.

SECTION 10. INDEMNIFICATION
10.1 Supplier shall defend Buyer against any third-party claim alleging that a deliverable infringes a patent, copyright or trademark, and pay any damages finally awarded or agreed in settlement.
10.2 The indemnified party shall give prompt notice of the claim, allow the indemnifying party to control its defense, and provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense.

SECTION 11. EXPENSES
11.1 Buyer shall reimburse Supplier for reasonable travel and out-of-pocket expenses that Buyer has approved in writing in advance, at cost and without mark-up, provided they comply with Buyer's travel policy as provided to Supplier.
11.2 Expense claims must be submitted within 180 days after the expense is incurred, with receipts for any single item above two hundred fifty dollars ($250).

SECTION 12. INFORMATION SECURITY
12.1 Supplier shall maintain administrative, physical and technical safeguards designed to protect Buyer's data, consistent with a recognized industry framework such as ISO/IEC 27001 or the NIST Cybersecurity Framework.
12.2 Supplier shall perform vulnerability scans of systems that process Buyer's data at least every 180 days and remediate critical findings within 20 days.

SECTION 13. CONFIDENTIALITY
13.1 Each party (the "Recipient") shall keep confidential all non-public information disclosed by the other party (the "Discloser") that is marked confidential or would reasonably be understood to be confidential ("Confidential Information"), and shall use it only to perform or receive the benefit of this Agreement.
13.2 The Recipient may disclose Confidential Information to its Personnel and professional advisers who need to know it and are bound by obligations of confidentiality no less protective than this Section.
13.3 These obligations continue for three (3) years after the expiration or termination of this Agreement, and for trade secrets for as long as they remain trade secrets under applicable law.
13.4 Within 45 days after a written request, the Recipient shall return or destroy the Discloser's Confidential Information, except for copies retained in routine backups or as required by law.

SECTION 14. INDEPENDENT CONTRACTORS
14.1 The parties are independent contractors. Nothing in this Agreement creates a partnership, joint venture, agency or employment relationship between them.

SECTION 15. ENTIRE AGREEMENT AND AMENDMENT
15.1 This Agreement, including its Schedules and each SOW, is the entire agreement of the parties on its subject and supersedes all prior proposals and understandings.
15.2 This Agreement may be amended only by a written instrument signed by authorized representatives of both parties.

SECTION 16. PERSONNEL AND SUBCONTRACTING
16.1 Supplier shall assign Personnel with the skills and experience reasonably required to perform the Services. Supplier may replace key Personnel named in an SOW only with Buyer's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
16.2 Supplier may use subcontractors only with Buyer's prior written consent. Supplier remains responsible for the acts and omissions of its subcontractors as if they were its own.
16.3 Supplier shall ensure that its Personnel comply with Buyer's reasonable site, security and safety rules when on Buyer's premises.

SECTION 17. TAXES
17.1 Fees exclude sales, use, value added and similar taxes. Buyer shall pay any such taxes that Supplier is required to collect, other than taxes on Supplier's net income, property or employees.
17.2 If Buyer is required by law to withhold tax from a payment, it shall pay the amount withheld to the relevant authority and provide Supplier with evidence of payment within 90 days.

SECTION 18. COUNTERPARTS
18.1 This Agreement may be signed in counterparts, including by electronic signature, each of which is an original and all of which together are one instrument.

SECTION 19. TERM AND RENEWAL
19.1 The initial term of this Agreement is eighteen (18) months from the Effective Date (the "Initial Term").
19.2 After the Initial Term, this Agreement renews automatically for successive periods of six (6) months each unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal at least thirty (30) days before the end of the then-current term.

SECTION 20. STATEMENTS OF WORK
20.1 The specific services, deliverables, milestones and fees for each engagement will be set out in a statement of work signed by authorized representatives of both parties (each, an "SOW"). Each SOW incorporates the terms of this Agreement.
20.2 Supplier shall not begin work under an SOW until it has been signed by both parties. Work performed before signature is at Supplier's own risk and expense.
20.3 Each SOW will identify a project manager for each party. The project managers will meet at least every 30 days to review progress, risks and open decisions.
20.4 If an SOW conflicts with this Agreement, this Agreement controls, unless the SOW expressly identifies by section number the provision of this Agreement that it overrides.

SECTION 21. VENUE
21.1 Each party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in Cook County, Illinois, for any action arising out of or relating to this Agreement, and waives any objection to venue in those courts.

SECTION 22. WARRANTIES
22.1 Supplier warrants that the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with generally accepted industry standards, and that each deliverable will conform in all material respects to its specifications for 10 days after acceptance.
22.2 Buyer's exclusive remedy for breach of the warranty in this Section is for Supplier to re-perform the non-conforming Services or, if Supplier cannot do so within a reasonable time, a refund of the fees paid for them.
22.3 EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY STATED IN THIS AGREEMENT, NEITHER PARTY MAKES ANY OTHER WARRANTY, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING ANY IMPLIED WARRANTY OF MERCHANTABILITY OR FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.

SECTION 23. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY
23.1 Neither party is liable for any indirect, incidental, special or consequential damages, or for lost profits, even if advised of their possibility.
23.2 Except for the excluded claims below, each party's aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the fees paid or payable by Buyer under this Agreement in the twenty-four (24) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.
23.3 The limitation above does not apply to a party's indemnification obligations or to its breach of the confidentiality obligations in this Agreement, for which that party's aggregate liability shall not exceed seven million five hundred thousand dollars ($7,500,000).

SECTION 24. EFFECT OF TERMINATION
24.1 On termination, Buyer shall pay all fees for Services performed through the effective date of termination, and each party shall return the other's Confidential Information as provided in this Agreement.
24.2 At Buyer's request, Supplier shall provide reasonable transition assistance for up to 180 days after termination, at the rates then in effect.

SECTION 25. COMPLIANCE WITH LAWS
25.1 Each party shall comply with all laws applicable to its performance of this Agreement, including anti-bribery laws and the export control and economic sanctions laws of the United States.
25.2 Neither party shall export, re-export or transfer any deliverable in violation of the export control laws of the United States or of any other applicable jurisdiction.

SECTION 26. GOVERNING LAW
26.1 This Agreement and any dispute arising out of it are governed by the laws of the State of Florida, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules.

SECTION 27. FORCE MAJEURE
27.1 Neither party is liable for any delay or failure to perform caused by events beyond its reasonable control, including fire, flood, war, epidemic, governmental action or failure of public utilities, provided it gives prompt notice and uses reasonable efforts to resume performance.
27.2 If a force majeure event prevents performance for more than 120 consecutive days, either party may terminate the affected SOW on written notice.

SECTION 28. DISPUTE ESCALATION
28.1 The parties shall first attempt to resolve any dispute through their project managers. If unresolved within 90 days, either party may escalate it to an executive of each party, who shall meet within a further 10 days.
28.2 Nothing in this Section prevents a party from seeking urgent injunctive relief.

SECTION 29. ACCEPTANCE
29.1 Buyer shall test each deliverable against the acceptance criteria in the applicable SOW within 15 Business Days of delivery and notify Supplier in writing of acceptance or of any non-conformity.
29.2 If Buyer reports a non-conformity, Supplier shall correct it and redeliver within 90 days, and the acceptance procedure shall be repeated. If a deliverable fails acceptance three (3) times, Buyer may terminate the applicable SOW and recover the fees paid for that deliverable.

SECTION 30. DATA PROTECTION
30.1 To the extent Supplier processes personal data on behalf of Buyer, it shall do so only on Buyer's documented instructions and in accordance with the data processing terms in Schedule D.
30.2 Supplier shall notify Buyer without undue delay, and in any event within 24 hours, after becoming aware of a security incident affecting Buyer's personal data.
30.3 Supplier shall retain Buyer's data for no longer than 20 days after the end of the applicable SOW, after which it shall securely delete that data unless retention is required by law.

SECTION 31. TERMINATION
31.1 Either party may terminate this Agreement or any SOW on written notice if the other party materially breaches it and fails to cure the breach within 15 days after receiving written notice describing it.
31.2 Either party may terminate this Agreement immediately on written notice if the other party becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, or has a receiver appointed for its business.
31.3 Buyer may terminate any SOW for convenience on 15 days' written notice, paying for Services performed up to the effective date of termination.

SECTION 32. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY
32.1 Upon payment in full of the applicable fees, Buyer shall own all deliverables created specifically for Buyer under an SOW, and Supplier hereby assigns to Buyer all rights in them.
32.2 Supplier retains all rights in its pre-existing materials, tools and know-how, and in any general improvements to them. To the extent any of them is incorporated in a deliverable, Supplier grants Buyer a perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use it as part of that deliverable.

SECTION 33. FEES AND INVOICING
33.1 Buyer shall pay all undisputed amounts within 15 days after the date of Supplier's invoice. Invoices shall be issued monthly in arrears unless an SOW states otherwise.
33.2 Amounts not paid when due bear interest at the lesser of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month and the highest rate permitted by law, from the due date until paid.
33.3 Buyer may withhold any amount it disputes in good faith by notifying Supplier of the dispute within 20 days of the invoice date, with reasonable detail of the reasons. The parties shall work together to resolve any dispute promptly.

TECHNOLOGY SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Technology Services Agreement (this "Agreement") is entered into as of December 26, 2022 (the "Effective Date") by and between Larkspur Foods LLP, a Colorado limited liability partnership ("Supplier"), and Marlow Retail Holdings LLP, a Delaware limited liability partnership ("Buyer").

RECITALS. Buyer wishes to obtain, and Supplier wishes to provide, the services described in this Agreement on the terms set out below.

SECTION 1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Personnel" means the employees, agents and permitted subcontractors of a party who perform obligations under this Agreement.
1.2 "Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or a day on which national banks in Chicago are authorized to close.
1.3 "Affiliate" means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a party, where "control" means ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting interests of the entity.
1.4 "Documentation" means the user guides, specifications and operating manuals that Supplier makes generally available for the Services, as updated from time to time.

SECTION 2. TAXES
2.1 Fees exclude sales, use, value added and similar taxes. Buyer shall pay any such taxes that Supplier is required to collect, other than taxes on Supplier's net income, property or employees.
2.2 If Buyer is required by law to withhold tax from a payment, it shall pay the amount withheld to the relevant authority and provide Supplier with evidence of payment within 45 days.

SECTION 3. CHANGE CONTROL
3.1 Either party may request a change to the scope, schedule or fees of an SOW by written change request. Supplier shall respond within 10 Business Days with an estimate of the impact on schedule and fees.
3.2 No change is binding until a change order describing it is signed by both parties. Supplier is not obliged to perform any change until that change order is signed.

SECTION 4. EFFECT OF TERMINATION
4.1 On termination, Buyer shall pay all fees for Services performed through the effective date of termination, and each party shall return the other's Confidential Information as provided in this Agreement.
4.2 At Buyer's request, Supplier shall provide reasonable transition assistance for up to 180 days after termination, at the rates then in effect.

SECTION 5. COUNTERPARTS
5.1 This Agreement may be signed in counterparts, including by electronic signature, each of which is an original and all of which together are one instrument.

SECTION 6. PUBLICITY
6.1 Neither party shall use the other's name or logo in any publicity, customer list or marketing material without the other's prior written consent.

SECTION 7. INFORMATION SECURITY
7.1 Supplier shall maintain administrative, physical and technical safeguards designed to protect Buyer's data, consistent with a recognized industry framework such as ISO/IEC 27001 or the NIST Cybersecurity Framework.
7.2 Supplier shall perform vulnerability scans of systems that process Buyer's data at least every 20 days and remediate critical findings within 60 days.

SECTION 8. WARRANTIES
8.1 Supplier warrants that the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with generally accepted industry standards, and that each deliverable will conform in all material respects to its specifications for 45 days after acceptance.
8.2 Buyer's exclusive remedy for breach of the warranty in this Section is for Supplier to re-perform the non-conforming Services or, if Supplier cannot do so within a reasonable time, a refund of the fees paid for them.
8.3 EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY STATED IN THIS AGREEMENT, NEITHER PARTY MAKES ANY OTHER WARRANTY, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING ANY IMPLIED WARRANTY OF MERCHANTABILITY OR FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.

SECTION 9. NON-SOLICITATION
9.1 During the term of this Agreement and for six (6) months after it ends, neither party shall solicit for employment any employee of the other party who was directly involved in performing this Agreement, except through general advertisements not targeted at such employees.

SECTION 10. FEES AND INVOICING
10.1 Buyer shall pay all undisputed amounts within 30 days after the date of Supplier's invoice. Invoices shall be issued monthly in arrears unless an SOW states otherwise.
10.2 Amounts not paid when due bear interest at the lesser of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month and the highest rate permitted by law, from the due date until paid.
10.3 Buyer may withhold any amount it disputes in good faith by notifying Supplier of the dispute within 30 days of the invoice date, with reasonable detail of the reasons. The parties shall work together to resolve any dispute promptly.

SECTION 11. INDEPENDENT CONTRACTORS
11.1 The parties are independent contractors. Nothing in this Agreement creates a partnership, joint venture, agency or employment relationship between them.

SECTION 12. VENUE
12.1 Each party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in Miami-Dade County, Florida, for any action arising out of or relating to this Agreement, and waives any objection to venue in those courts.

SECTION 13. DATA PROTECTION
13.1 To the extent Supplier processes personal data on behalf of Buyer, it shall do so only on Buyer's documented instructions and in accordance with the data processing terms in Schedule D.
13.2 Supplier shall notify Buyer without undue delay, and in any event within 24 hours, after becoming aware of a security incident affecting Buyer's personal data.
13.3 Supplier shall retain Buyer's data for no longer than 10 days after the end of the applicable SOW, after which it shall securely delete that data unless retention is required by law.

SECTION 14. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY
14.1 Upon payment in full of the applicable fees, Buyer shall own all deliverables created specifically for Buyer under an SOW, and Supplier hereby assigns to Buyer all rights in them.
14.2 Supplier retains all rights in its pre-existing materials, tools and know-how, and in any general improvements to them. To the extent any of them is incorporated in a deliverable, Supplier grants Buyer a perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use it as part of that deliverable.

SECTION 15. SEVERABILITY AND WAIVER
15.1 If any provision of this Agreement is held invalid, the remaining provisions remain in effect. A failure to enforce a provision is not a waiver of it.

SECTION 16. ACCEPTANCE
16.1 Buyer shall test each deliverable against the acceptance criteria in the applicable SOW within 10 Business Days of delivery and notify Supplier in writing of acceptance or of any non-conformity.
16.2 If Buyer reports a non-conformity, Supplier shall correct it and redeliver within 45 days, and the acceptance procedure shall be repeated. If a deliverable fails acceptance three (3) times, Buyer may terminate the applicable SOW and recover the fees paid for that deliverable.

SECTION 17. CONFIDENTIALITY
17.1 Each party (the "Recipient") shall keep confidential all non-public information disclosed by the other party (the "Discloser") that is marked confidential or would reasonably be understood to be confidential ("Confidential Information"), and shall use it only to perform or receive the benefit of this Agreement.
17.2 The Recipient may disclose Confidential Information to its Personnel and professional advisers who need to know it and are bound by obligations of confidentiality no less protective than this Section.
17.3 These obligations continue for five (5) years after the expiration or termination of this Agreement, and for trade secrets for as long as they remain trade secrets under applicable law.
17.4 Within 20 days after a written request, the Recipient shall return or destroy the Discloser's Confidential Information, except for copies retained in routine backups or as required by law.

SECTION 18. ENTIRE AGREEMENT AND AMENDMENT
18.1 This Agreement, including its Schedules and each SOW, is the entire agreement of the parties on its subject and supersedes all prior proposals and understandings.
18.2 This Agreement may be amended only by a written instrument signed by authorized representatives of both parties.

SECTION 19. TERM AND RENEWAL
19.1 The initial term of this Agreement begins on the Effective Date and ends on December 25, 2024 (the "Initial Term").
19.2 After the Initial Term, this Agreement renews automatically for successive periods of six (6) months each unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal at least forty-five (45) days before the end of the then-current term.

SECTION 20. FORCE MAJEURE
20.1 Neither party is liable for any delay or failure to perform caused by events beyond its reasonable control, including fire, flood, war, epidemic, governmental action or failure of public utilities, provided it gives prompt notice and uses reasonable efforts to resume performance.
20.2 If a force majeure event prevents performance for more than 10 consecutive days, either party may terminate the affected SOW on written notice.

SECTION 21. AUDIT
21.1 Buyer may, on 90 days' written notice and no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, audit Supplier's records relating to fees charged under this Agreement.
21.2 Supplier shall keep those records for at least three (3) years after the fees are invoiced. If an audit shows an overcharge of more than five percent (5%), Supplier shall bear the reasonable cost of the audit.

SECTION 22. STATEMENTS OF WORK
22.1 The specific services, deliverables, milestones and fees for each engagement will be set out in a statement of work signed by authorized representatives of both parties (each, an "SOW"). Each SOW incorporates the terms of this Agreement.
22.2 Supplier shall not begin work under an SOW until it has been signed by both parties. Work performed before signature is at Supplier's own risk and expense.
22.3 Each SOW will identify a project manager for each party. The project managers will meet at least every 14 days to review progress, risks and open decisions.
22.4 If an SOW conflicts with this Agreement, this Agreement controls, unless the SOW expressly identifies by section number the provision of this Agreement that it overrides.

SECTION 23. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY
23.1 Neither party is liable for any indirect, incidental, special or consequential damages, or for lost profits, even if advised of their possibility.
23.2 Except for the excluded claims below, each party's aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) two million dollars ($2,000,000) and (b) the fees paid or payable by Buyer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.
23.3 The limitation above does not apply to a party's indemnification obligations or to its breach of the confidentiality obligations in this Agreement, for which that party's aggregate liability shall not exceed five million dollars ($5,000,000).

SECTION 24. NOTICES
24.1 Notices under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered by hand, by nationally recognized overnight courier, or by email with confirmation of receipt, to the addresses set out on the signature page or as later updated by notice.
24.2 A notice is effective on receipt, or if delivered by courier, 1 Business Day(s) after dispatch.

SECTION 25. EXPENSES
25.1 Buyer shall reimburse Supplier for reasonable travel and out-of-pocket expenses that Buyer has approved in writing in advance, at cost and without mark-up, provided they comply with Buyer's travel policy as provided to Supplier.
25.2 Expense claims must be submitted within 180 days after the expense is incurred, with receipts for any single item above two hundred fifty dollars ($250).

SECTION 26. GOVERNING LAW
26.1 This Agreement and any dispute arising out of it are governed by the laws of the State of Florida, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules.

SECTION 27. COMPLIANCE WITH LAWS
27.1 Each party shall comply with all laws applicable to its performance of this Agreement, including anti-bribery laws and the export control and economic sanctions laws of the United States.
27.2 Neither party shall export, re-export or transfer any deliverable in violation of the export control laws of the United States or of any other applicable jurisdiction.

SECTION 28. INDEMNIFICATION
28.1 Supplier shall defend Buyer against any third-party claim alleging that a deliverable infringes a patent, copyright or trademark, and pay any damages finally awarded or agreed in settlement.
28.2 The indemnified party shall give prompt notice of the claim, allow the indemnifying party to control its defense, and provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense.

SECTION 29. INSURANCE
29.1 Supplier shall maintain, with insurers rated A- or better, commercial general liability insurance of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000) per occurrence, professional liability insurance of at least three million dollars ($3,000,000) per claim, and workers' compensation insurance as required by law.
29.2 Supplier shall provide certificates of insurance on request and give Buyer at least 20 days' notice before any required policy is cancelled or materially reduced.

SECTION 30. ASSIGNMENT
30.1 Neither party may assign this Agreement without the other party's prior written consent, except to an Affiliate or to a successor to all or substantially all of its business to which this Agreement relates, on written notice to the other party.

SECTION 31. PERSONNEL AND SUBCONTRACTING
31.1 Supplier shall assign Personnel with the skills and experience reasonably required to perform the Services. Supplier may replace key Personnel named in an SOW only with Buyer's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
31.2 Supplier may use subcontractors only with Buyer's prior written consent. Supplier remains responsible for the acts and omissions of its subcontractors as if they were its own.
31.3 Supplier shall ensure that its Personnel comply with Buyer's reasonable site, security and safety rules when on Buyer's premises.

SECTION 32. TERMINATION
32.1 Either party may terminate this Agreement or any SOW on written notice if the other party materially breaches it and fails to cure the breach within 180 days after receiving written notice describing it.
32.2 Either party may terminate this Agreement immediately on written notice if the other party becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, or has a receiver appointed for its business.
32.3 Buyer may terminate any SOW for convenience on 45 days' written notice, paying for Services performed up to the effective date of termination.

SECTION 33. DISPUTE ESCALATION
33.1 The parties shall first attempt to resolve any dispute through their project managers. If unresolved within 15 days, either party may escalate it to an executive of each party, who shall meet within a further 45 days.
33.2 Nothing in this Section prevents a party from seeking urgent injunctive relief.
